jobs.description:
About Club Capital and the youth sports business

Club Capital is an accounting, tax, and CFO advisory firm that serves insurance agencies and youth sports clubs. We work with roughly 1,000 clients firmwide, about 50 of them youth sports clubs, and each one is matched with a credentialed accountant or controller who knows their business. This role sits on the youth sports side.

Our youth sports clients are organizations run as businesses, and we support the business side of each one: accounting, tax, and compliance. Most are 501(c)(3) nonprofits managed by a volunteer board of directors, most of whom are parents of current players. A smaller share are for-profit entities owned by a founder or head coach. They collect registration, tournament, and sponsorship revenue and pay coaches as employees or contractors, which creates exempt-organization filings, payroll tax and 1099 reporting, and sales and use tax obligations in the states where they operate.

About the role

You own all tax for the non-profit side of our youth sports practice. Every tax client is also a controller and/or CFO services client of ours. We do not handle tax filings for any entity or individual whose business or club is not with us for accounting or advisory work. Your work starts with tax onboarding: working out which returns have been filed, whether the client is current, which accounting method they say they use and whether it matches the books, what resolution items are open, and what questions they have. From there, you manage the recurring tax work that keeps each client current. You also handle returns for our for-profit clubs and individual 1040s, mostly for club owners and executive directors.

What we hold this role to:

  • Every new client onboarded with filing history confirmed, accounting method matched to the books, and open resolution items identified.
  • Every 990 filed or extended on time, and every 1099 filed by its deadline.
  • Federal, state, and payroll notices answered well before their response deadlines.
  • Clients who know where they stand on sales tax and payroll tax.

What you'll do

  • Own the process. Create, refine, and hold to the process around the recurring tax work. If the process fails, you have failed. Our youth sports accountants and controllers keep the books, so you partner with them at every step and present a unified front to the client, in plain English.
  • Manage the 990 cycle. Manage the preparation of Forms 990, 990-EZ, and 990-N, plus Form 990-T where unrelated business income applies, and review and sign the returns. Handle state charitable registrations and annual filings, and file the extensions for every return that needs one. Get the governance, compensation, and program service answers right, because the public reads them.
  • Own the annual 1099 process. Set the timeline, coordinate with the accounting team and the client, prepare all forms, and meet every deadline.
  • Own sales and use tax and franchise tax. Work out what is taxable for each club by state, manage registrations and exemption certificates, prepare and file sales and use tax returns and state franchise tax filings, and answer state inquiries.
  • Own tax resolution. Resolve federal, state, and payroll notices: triage what comes in, research it, respond, and request penalty relief where it is warranted. Handle payment plans, delinquent filings, and representation before the IRS and state agencies as part of that work. Keep powers of attorney current so clients never have to deal with the IRS or a state agency alone.
  • Own payroll tax items. Review 941, 940, state withholding, and unemployment filings, reconcile W-2 reporting, and settle coach classification questions before they become notices.
  • Prepare for-profit and individual returns. Prepare business returns for our for-profit clubs and 1040s for club owners and executive directors.
  • Provide tax planning and advisory. Meet with clients to discuss their tax strategy, explain what a number on a 990 means and how to protect exempt status, and work with the accounting team so the books stay in alignment with that strategy.

What we're looking for

Required

  • An active CPA or EA license in good standing
  • Experience managing and reviewing Forms 990 for tax-exempt organizations
  • Experience with tax resolution, including resolving IRS and state tax notices
  • Working knowledge of payroll tax filings, including Forms 941 and 940 and state withholding and unemployment
  • Experience managing the full 1099 process: setting timelines, coordinating with accounting teams and clients, preparing all forms, and meeting every deadline
  • Comfort preparing business returns and 1040s
  • The ability to explain tax issues clearly to volunteer board members and small-business owners

Preferred

  • A CPA license
  • Experience with sales and use tax across more than one state
  • Experience with state charitable registrations and franchise tax filings
  • Experience with Form 990-T and unrelated business income
  • Experience with youth sports, schools, or other membership-based nonprofits
  • Experience in a high-volume practice with a large client base
  • Familiarity with Intuit ProConnect, TaxDome, and QuickBooks

How we work

Most of our deadlines are nonprofit deadlines, which vary by each client's registered fiscal year.

We work in Intuit ProConnect for returns, TaxDome for client workflow, e-signatures, and powers of attorney, and QuickBooks for the books. You will work alongside our youth sports accountants and controllers, who each carry a small, defined set of clients, so you will know both the people and the books behind every return.

Reports to: Director of Tax (dotted line to VP of Youth Sports)

jobs.excerpt: About RunwareRunware is the AI inference platform that builds and runs its own infrastructure, end to end.
jobs.description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and runs its own infrastructure, end to end. Our Sonic Inference Engine has served more than 20 billion requests for over 1 million developers and 500 million end users, with 400,000+ models behind a single integration, at up to 10x lower cost per token than traditional providers.

We are now building the AI Factory that runs it. The Sonic Inference Pod packs 1 MW of custom-designed compute into a 20-foot container with closed-loop, water-free cooling, sited wherever power exists. Pods are live in the US and Europe, and we are scaling to dozens of pods and tens of thousands of GPUs, all operated as one distributed fabric that reroutes traffic the moment a pod goes offline (announcement).

Every one of those pods holds customer models, customer data and millions of dollars of GPUs, sometimes inside a customer's own perimeter or a sovereign jurisdiction. Keeping all of it secure without slowing anyone down is the job.

The role

As Senior Security Engineer, you will own the security of Runware's AI supercomputer: the bare-metal GPU fleet, the Sonic Inference Pods it lives in, the managed Kubernetes clusters we hand to customers, and the control plane that ties it all together across the US and Europe. You will design the controls, build the first version with your own hands, and set the standard for how security is run across every pod.

This is a hands-on senior individual-contributor role. You will threat-model a new pod before it ships, harden the image that every GPU node boots from, prove to an enterprise customer's security team that their model weights never leave their tenant, and when something goes wrong, lead the response and fix the root cause so it never happens again. You will work directly with our CISO, with the inference engine, platform and hardware teams, and with the site teams deploying pods.

Success means a customer workload on a shared pod is isolated as strongly as on a dedicated one, no human has a standing login to a production node, every change to the fleet is reviewed, signed and auditable, and an enterprise security review takes days instead of months.

What you'll do

  • Own the security architecture of the fleet: host hardening for bare-metal GPU nodes, immutable images and a signed build pipeline, boot integrity, and the identity, secrets and access model for humans and services across every pod.
  • Secure multi-tenancy on shared infrastructure. Design and verify isolation between customer workloads at the network, Kubernetes, host and GPU layers, and produce the evidence that proves it holds.
  • Secure the managed Kubernetes offering: cluster hardening, admission control, RBAC, supply-chain controls for images, and a clean, auditable handover of clusters to customers.
  • Build security visibility across the fleet: logging, detection, alerting and audit trails from firmware to API, wired into the fleet dashboards and on-call so that an anomaly on one node in one pod is seen within minutes.
  • Lead security reviews and threat models for new pods, sites, servers and platform features, with a focus on real-world risk rather than checklists.
  • Run incident response for the infrastructure: investigation, containment, recovery and post-incident learning, as part of the on-call rotation.
  • Own vulnerability management for the fleet: firmware, kernel, drivers, GPU stack and container images across thousands of nodes, with a patch cadence you can defend to a customer.
  • Answer enterprise customers' security due diligence with engineering evidence, and partner with the CISO on the SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls that touch the infrastructure.
  • Design for sovereign and on-premise deployments: data residency, in-country key management, and physical and remote-access controls for a pod sitting on a customer's site.
  • Use AI to accelerate the work: automate evidence collection, log triage, configuration audits and runbooks with LLM-based agents, so that a very small team can secure a very large fleet.

Requirements

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years in security or infrastructure engineering, with several of those securing production infrastructure at a company that runs its own hardware at scale.
  • A track record of building security controls, not just auditing them. You have taken a hardening standard, an access model or a detection pipeline from design to running across a fleet, and you know what breaks between the two.
  • Deep, current, hands-on Linux security expertise: kernel hardening, namespaces and cgroups, seccomp, eBPF, secure and measured boot, TPM-based attestation, and the tooling to see exactly what a process did.
  • Strong Kubernetes security: RBAC, admission control and policy engines, network policy, runtime security, image signing and SBOMs, and the ways a container escapes.
  • Fluent in network security on real hardware: segmentation and VLAN or VXLAN isolation, firewalls, out-of-band management networks, and the risks that live in BMC, IPMI and switch management planes.
  • Experience with identity, secrets and PKI at scale: short-lived credentials, workload identity, hardware-backed keys, and removing standing access without slowing engineers down.
  • Fluent in Python or Go, and comfortable writing the tooling, scanners and automation yourself rather than waiting for someone else to.
  • You use AI to accelerate your own output every day, for scripting, log analysis, code review, documentation and incident triage, and you have a clear view of how a small security team armed with these tools should operate differently.
  • A clear communicator who can explain the same trade-off to an engineer, a customer's CISO and a founder in one afternoon, and who assesses risk pragmatically rather than by the book.

Nice to have

CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. About Claude Corps

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career talent in nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions those organizations can continue using after the fellowship ends. You’ll lead the Claude Corps screener team day to day. You make sure applications are reviewed, screens are completed, and every candidate decision is documented on time.

The Director sets recruiting strategy and cohort hiring goals. You turn those goals into weekly targets, plan staffing, and manage the team’s work. This is a hands-on management role. You train and coach screeners, review their work, and keep selection standards consistent as volume grows. You work closely with the Director, the recruiting coordinator, and the Claude Corps program team.

Run screening delivery

Maintain clear selection standards

Key Success Metrics

  • Weekly delivery: Application reviews and screens meet agreed targets, and delays and staffing gaps are flagged early

  • Screener readiness: New screeners are trained in time for cohort needs and meet the team’s standards

  • Team performance: Screeners get regular feedback, and performance issues are addressed promptly

  • You have managed a team’s workload, output, and quality using weekly targets and reporting
  • You have trained people to apply consistent selection standards and can explain how you checked their decisions

jobs.excerpt: Grow our AI image service. Before you apply, spend ten minutes on our website and LinkedIn.
jobs.description:
Grow our AI image service.

Before you apply, spend ten minutes on our website and LinkedIn. In your Loom we will ask what we do, where you found out about us, and why you want to work at Drop Zero Digital. Answers that could be about any company will not pass.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years. We check your work history against what you tell us, and a false answer ends the application.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video. Research us first.
  2. A short test by email: one real decision task, your internet speed, your computer, and a paragraph on your work history.
  3. A 15 minute call with the founder.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. Aptitude tests. These inform us, they do not decide.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Based in Uruguay.

Benefits

2100 USD per month from day one, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus.
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

jobs.excerpt: Lateral stands for technology excellence.  We’re a profitable, award-winning design and technology company with over 20 years of experience launching bold ventures and transforming businesses.
jobs.description:
Lateral stands for technology excellence.

We’re a profitable, award-winning design and technology company with over 20 years of experience launching bold ventures and transforming businesses. A globally distributed team of 200+ experts united by a shared purpose: the continuous pursuit of quality.

Our clients come to us for results, quality and craft - and stay because we keep raising the bar.

We Do Things Differently at Lateral

Our mission is simple: design and build great products.
What sets us apart isn’t just the talent of our team - it’s the way we work:

We Have A Bias For Action & Results.

We are doers - we spot the gaps, connect the dots, anticipate what’s around the corner and take action. We move fast, stay focused, and let the results - not the effort - speak for themselves.

We Work On Time, On Budget, On Quality

Discipline is our edge - a commitment we make to each other, to our clients, and to the standards we hold ourselves to.

We Care Deeply.

We care about our work and about each other. Care Is A Competitive Advantage.

Every detail matters. Every design, every line of code, every decision. Thoughtful by default.

We Do Things Right - Because It’s the Right Thing to Do

Right over easy. Integrity isn’t up for negotiation. We hold the bar high even when no one’s watching. We take pride in doing great work the right way - not the easy way.

We Keep Improving

The best teams keep improving and we’re never done learning.

We iterate. We reflect on what’s working and what’s not. Feedback fuels us, we receive it openly, and adapt quickly. Progress over perfection.

We’re Obsessed With Agility, Not The Agile Manifesto

We don’t chase dogma or rituals - we chase momentum. We adapt processes to fit problems, not the other way around.

We Take Ownership
Everyone leads something here. You will have room to run with ideas, and the trust to execute. That trust is built on how you show up: thinking things through, sweating the details, and following through.

What You'll Do

As a Solutions Architect at Lateral, your role is to connect business ambition with the technology needed to deliver it. You will shape solutions, guide technical direction, and partner directly with clients, while supporting our delivery teams with clarity, structure, and sound architectural judgment.

You will:

  • Lead solution definition for key initiatives: architecture, technical approach, integration strategy, cloud alignment, and delivery feasibility.

  • Work directly with client executives and product leaders to translate business needs into scalable, modern architectures across AWS, Azure,orGCP.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to turn architectural direction into actionable plans, balancing quality, velocity, and pragmatic tradeoffs.

  • Conduct architecture assessments, review existing systems, and define modernization, migration, or greenfield approaches.

  • Develop solution proposals, SOWs, estimates, and architectural documentation for pre-sales and delivery.

  • Represent Lateral in early conversations with hyperscalers. As part of a strategic initiative, you’ll help build partner relationships with AWS, Azure, and GCP.

  • Support delivery teams through ongoing architectural decisions, technical guidance, and risk identification.

  • Champion clarity and quality: ensuring our solutions are maintainable, well-structured, secure, and aligned with long-term business value.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for a seasoned architect with a consulting mindset, someone who is equally strong in technical depth, stakeholder communication, and problem framing.

You must bring:

  • 7+ years of experience in technical leadership roles such as Solutions Architect, Senior Architect, Principal Consultant, or similar.

  • A background in consulting or services environments

  • Deep expertise in designing systems on AWS, Azure,orGCP architecture patterns, compute, storage, API design, integration strategies, observability, and deployment models.

  • Strong ability to lead discovery conversations, clarify requirements, and translate business needs into technical direction.

  • Experience shaping architecture for complex systems, SaaS products, integrations, distributed systems, and modern cloud applications.

  • Excellent communication skills: you can explain tradeoffs, options, and decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Strong consultancy instincts: pre-sales exposure, client advisory work, and solution packaging are second nature to you.

  • A preference for modern software engineering (cloud-native, serverless, event-driven, container-based, or hybrid approaches).

  • Comfort working in ambiguity, shaping clarity, and bringing structure to complex technical and business problems.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Real Impact: You’ll work on meaningful products that make a measurable difference - from healthcare and commerce to sustainability and next-gen tech.

  • Remote-First, Office Friendly: Work from wherever you’re most productive - whether that’s your home, a co-working space, or one of our offices. We’re a remote-first company, but if you’re near an office, you’re welcome to drop in, collaborate in person, or work onsite regularly.

    We prioritize async collaboration, respect your time zone, and focus on outcomes over hours.

  • An Outstanding Team: Talented, kind, and hard-working people who care deeply about their craft - and about each other. No egos. No politics. Just professionals doing their best work.

  • Growth: You’ll be supported in growing your craft, exploring new paths, and stepping into greater responsibility - at your own pace

  • A Culture of Excellence: We care deeply about doing the right thing - for our clients, our team, and ourselves. No burnout. No crunch. Just high-quality work, delivered sustainably.

  • Variety & Stability: We’re profitable, independent, and over a decade strong. Yet every project brings a fresh challenge. You’ll never be bored here.

This Role Might Not Be for You

We want to respect your time by being clear about what this role isn’t. You should skip this opportunity if:

  • You prefer well defined structure. If you gravitate towards a clear hierarchy, well defined roles and swim lanes, you may find our self-managed style challenging.

  • Distributed work isn’t your thing. If you find async communication, design documentation and being proactive without a manager nearby difficult, our setup won’t suit you.

  • Feedback doesn't excite you. We’re obsessed with quality and believe in continuous improvement. That means we give feedback that’s sometimes nitpicky. If refining the work until it’s excellent feels over the top, you are likely going to find working here frustrating.

  • Change makes you uncomfortable. We’re scaling and maturing. That means not everything is perfect yet. Priorities shift. Processes evolve. If ambiguity is uncomfortable, this may feel bumpy.

However, If this sounds like fuel, we’d love to talk!

How to apply and what to expect in the interview process

01. Your work
Show us the work that reflects you at your best. We’ll look at depth, design thinking, and the logic behind your choices.

02. Lateral team fit
You’ll speak with our Talent team about your career direction, your motivators, and our plans ahead.

03. Work trial

You’ll tackle a take-home challenge that mirrors what we actually do.

04.Engineering deep dive
A collaborative session with our engineers.

05. Project fit
An interview focussed on prioritization, collaboration across disciplines, and how you handle the "messy middle".

Req ID:397038

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a SAP S/4HANA Cutover Lead / Deployment & Go-Live Lead- Remote to join our team in Ottawa, Ontario (CA-ON), Canada (CA).

SAP S/4HANA Cutover Lead / Deployment & Go-Live Lead

Experience: 10+ years of overall IT/SAP experience
Role Type: Senior Lead
Start Date: ASAP

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced SAP Cutover Lead to lead the end-to-end planning, coordination, and execution of cutover activities for a complex SAP transformation program.

In this role, you will oversee the transition from legacy systems to SAP, ensuring all business and technology activities are properly planned, coordinated, and executed for a successful go-live. This includes developing the cutover strategy, managing detailed execution runbooks, leading cutover rehearsals, coordinating production deployment, overseeing command-center activities, and supporting post-go-live stabilization.

You will work closely with business stakeholders, SAP functional and technical teams, data migration, integration, infrastructure, security, testing, reporting, change management, and third-party vendors to deliver a controlled and timely deployment while minimizing disruption to critical business operations.

The ideal candidate brings significant experience leading complex SAP deployments, with a strong understanding of SAP cutover planning, data migration, integrations, production readiness, go/no-go governance, and hypercare. Experience with SAP S/4HANA and large-scale, multi-site or multi-country implementations is highly desirable.

Key Responsibilities

1. Cutover Strategy & Planning

  • Develop and maintain the overall SAP cutover strategy, integrated cutover plan, detailed schedule, and execution runbook.
  • Translate deployment requirements into clearly defined cutover activities, including owners, timelines, dependencies, prerequisites, and completion criteria.
  • Establish entry and exit criteria, decision points, escalation paths, rollback procedures, and contingency plans.
  • Identify critical-path activities and ensure dependencies across business and technology workstreams are properly sequenced.
  • Maintain an integrated view of all activities required before, during, and immediately following SAP go-live.

2. Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Coordinate cutover activities across the following areas:
    • SAP functional modules and workstreams
    • Business functions
    • Data migration and conversion
    • Interfaces and integrations
    • Infrastructure and environments
    • Security and user access
    • Reporting and analytics
    • Testing and validation
    • Batch jobs and scheduling
    • Third-party applications and vendors
    • Business readiness and operational support
  • Work closely with the IT Technical Lead, SAP functional and technical leads, business stakeholders, project managers, and implementation partners.
  • Ensure clear ownership and accountability for every cutover activity.

3. Cutover Rehearsals & Readiness

  • Plan and lead cutover rehearsals, mock cutovers, dress rehearsals, and production-readiness exercises.
  • Facilitate cutover planning workshops and readiness-review meetings.
  • Document rehearsal results, identify gaps and bottlenecks, and incorporate lessons learned into subsequent cutover plans.
  • Validate that critical activities can be completed within the required production cutover window.
  • Lead readiness assessments and ensure outstanding issues are resolved or formally accepted before go-live.

4. Go-Live Governance

  • Establish and manage go/no-go criteria and governance checkpoints.
  • Facilitate go/no-go meetings with business and technology leadership.
  • Ensure critical risks, dependencies, defects, data issues, infrastructure readiness, and support requirements are understood before production deployment.
  • Maintain decision, action, risk, issue, and dependency logs.
  • Provide concise status reporting and promptly escalate blockers and critical risks.

5. Production Cutover Execution

  • Lead execution of the approved cutover plan during the production deployment window.
  • Coordinate technical and business teams through each stage of the cutover.
  • Track activities against the integrated cutover runbook in real time.
  • Manage deviations from the approved plan and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Facilitate command-center or war-room meetings during critical cutover periods.
  • Ensure decisions, exceptions, issues, and resolutions are accurately documented.

6. Data Migration & Technical Coordination

  • Coordinate data extraction, transformation, loading, reconciliation, and business validation activities.
  • Ensure data migration activities are properly sequenced with SAP configuration, integrations, interfaces, and business processes.
  • Coordinate system access, security provisioning, interface transitions, batch schedules, and technical validation.
  • Ensure critical integrations and business processes are validated before and after go-live.
  • Work closely with technical teams to resolve cutover-related defects and dependencies.

7. Post-Go-Live Stabilization & Hypercare

  • Coordinate early-life support and hypercare activities following SAP go-live.
  • Ensure incidents, defects, outstanding cutover activities, and operational issues have clearly assigned owners and resolution timelines.
  • Monitor stabilization progress and escalate critical production issues.
  • Coordinate the transition from the project/cutover organization to application support and operational teams.
  • Ensure operational procedures, support coverage, documentation, and escalation processes are established.

8. Continuous Improvement

  • Conduct post-cutover reviews and document lessons learned.
  • Identify opportunities to improve cutover methodologies, governance, templates, controls, and execution practices.
  • Develop reusable cutover frameworks and best practices for future SAP releases and deployments.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • 10+ years of overall IT/SAP experience, with significant experience in enterprise application deployment, cutover, or go-live management.
  • 7+ years of proven experience as a Cutover Lead, Deployment Lead, Go-Live Lead, or in a similar role on complex SAP programs.
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting SAP implementations, upgrades, migrations, or major releases.
  • Strong experience developing and managing detailed cutover plans, schedules, runbooks, dependency maps, and readiness checklists.
  • Demonstrated experience leading cutover rehearsals, production deployments, command centers, go/no-go meetings, and hypercare activities.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • SAP implementation lifecycle
    • Data migration and reconciliation
    • Enterprise integrations and interfaces
    • Testing and validation
    • Infrastructure and production environments
    • Security and access management
    • Change management
    • Production support and hypercare
  • Proven ability to coordinate complex activities across business teams, IT, implementation partners, and third-party vendors.
  • Strong RAID management, governance, and executive-status reporting capabilities.
  • Excellent facilitation, communication, organizational, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to make sound decisions, manage escalations, and coordinate large teams under significant time pressure.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with SAP S/4HANA implementations or migrations.
  • Experience leading multiple mock cutovers or cutover rehearsals ahead of production deployment.
  • Experience with large-scale multi-site, multi-country, or global SAP deployments.
  • Experience coordinating SAP deployments involving multiple legacy applications and complex integration landscapes.
  • Experience working with geographically distributed business and technology teams.
  • Experience in highly regulated or complex enterprise environments is an advantage.

Key Skills & Competencies

SAP Cutover Management | SAP S/4HANA | Deployment Planning | Go-Live Management | Cutover Runbook | Cutover Rehearsals | Mock Cutover | Data Migration | Data Reconciliation | SAP Integrations | Production Readiness | Go/No-Go Governance | Command Center | Hypercare | RAID Management | Dependency Management | Business Readiness | Stakeholder Management | Production Support

About Sibros Technologies

Who We Are

Sibros is accelerating the future of SDV excellence with its Deep Connected Platform™ that orchestrates full vehicle software update management, vehicle analytics, and remote commands in one integrated system. Adaptable to any vehicle architecture, Sibros’ platform meets stringent safety, security, and compliance standards, propelling OEMs to innovate new connected vehicle use cases across fleet management, predictive maintenance, data monetization, and beyond.

Our Mission

Our mission is to help our customers get the most value out of their connected devices.

Follow us on

LinkedIn | Youtube | Instagram

About the Role:

Job Title: Senior Manager (Software Solutions Architecture)

Location: Remote, India

Job Type: Full-Time

Experience: 10+ years, including 4+ years managing engineers

You will travel to prospective and existing OEM customers and design how their systems connect to the Sibros Deep Connected Platform: vehicle-to-cloud connectivity, data pipelines, OTA update programs, and the integration points into their own manufacturing and after-sales systems. You are the person the customer's engineering leadership talks to when they need to know how this will actually work in their environment.

From design to delivery, your team sits at every step of the customer engagement and owns what comes out of it: the Sibros platform running inside the customer's own cloud account, with Sibros keeping ownership and day-to-day management of the environment, plus the customer-specific solutions that let the platform interface with an OEM's manufacturing and after-sales processes. You design the solutions that bring our product platform and our customers' requirements together. As part of the Infrastructure department, you help keep that platform performing reliably and at scale.

What You'll Do

  • Own the customer architecture. Act as the primary technical contact for OEM accounts and prospects. Travel on site to run architecture workshops, technical deep dives, and the executive conversations that follow them.
  • Design the integration. Architect how a customer's vehicle programs, cloud estate, and enterprise systems connect to the Deep Connected Platform, and make sure the design holds up against their security, compliance, and data residency requirements.
  • Support pre-sales. Lead proof-of-concept engagements, architecture reviews, and RFP responses, and carry them through to a design that can be deployed rather than one that only reads well.
  • Run the Customer Hosted team. Manage the engineers who deploy and operate the Sibros platform inside customer cloud accounts, where we keep ownership of the service without owning the account it runs in.
  • Deliver custom solutions. Direct the design and delivery of customer-specific work built within the platform, using AI-assisted development tooling to keep delivery fast without giving up quality.
  • Grow the team. Hire, coach, and set direction, and stay technical enough to be a genuine reference for your engineers rather than only their manager.
  • Work across Sibros. Partner with Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, and Customer Success to turn a customer's business objectives into something we can build and operate.

What You Should Know

Basic Qualifications

  • Experience. 10+ years across software engineering, cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, networking, and security.
  • People management. 4+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring and performance responsibility.
  • Architecture. 5+ years designing, implementing, or consulting on complex cloud architectures, with production deployments behind you.
  • Hands-on infrastructure. Strong Kubernetes and Terraform. You should be able to review your team's work on a customer-hosted deployment and recognise when the answer is wrong.
  • Cloud. Working knowledge of at least one major hyperscaler (AWS or GCP), and of deploying into an environment you do not control, under someone else's security and compliance rules.
  • Communication. Able to explain the same design to a customer's VP of Engineering and to the engineer who has to build it, and be understood by both.
  • Travel. Willing to travel internationally to customer sites on a regular basis.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Connected vehicle, SDV, or automotive telematics background.
  • Hands-on experience integrating cloud-native platforms with OEM enterprise backends (PLM, MES, SAP, after-sales).
  • Experience running software in a customer-controlled environment, where you own the service but not the account.
  • Familiarity with multi-region delivery across regions, and the requirements that differ between them.
  • Comfortable using LLM-based tooling in daily engineering work. Experience with Claude Code is a bonus.
  • Real-time and batch processing using technologies such as MQTT, Kafka, Kubernetes, time-series databases, and the analytics tooling on top of them, applied to connected vehicles or comparable IoT workloads.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation package with performance incentives.
  • A dynamic work environment with a flat hierarchy and the opportunity for rapid career advancement.
  • Access to continuous learning and development opportunities.
  • Flexible working hours to accommodate different time zones.
  • Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance and wellness programs.
  • A culture that values innovation and promotes a work-life balance.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We're looking for an M&A Intern to join manda, iwoca's M&A platform. This is a paid off-cycle internship of up to 6 months, for someone who wants to build a long-term career in fintech - Hybrid in London.

manda is where AI meets Mergers & Acquisitions. Over the last months we've built a proposition for buying and selling UK small businesses. Our first deals are done, and our pipeline is growing across both sell-side and buy-side. Most M&A firms shy away from the sub-£10m EV segment because information asymmetry, lack of knowledge, and low transaction sizes make it hard to serve profitably. iwoca has 150,000+ SME customers in the UK and a track record of building clean, automated processes, and manda is leveraging that to build an M&A platform that serves this market properly.

Your edge as an intern: you'll work on live sub-£10m transactions from week one, not pitch books for deals you'll never touch. You'll see the full deal lifecycle (origination, diligence, execution, close) inside a venture small enough that the work you do moves the business, and you'll have AI and automation as leverage rather than as a side project.

The team

You'll sit inside the manda Deal Team and work directly with the people running the platform: our sell-side and buy-side Transaction Managers, our Due Diligence Manager, and the Venture Lead. The team is small enough that you'll be in the room for real decisions on live deals, and the tooling we use (CRM, VDR, AI automated workflows) is being built in parallel by the same people you'll be working alongside.

The role

The internship is split into two phases to give you both breadth across the deal engine and depth on a project you own.

Phase 1: Core M&A Operations (first 2 months). You'll get to try out several of our live workstreams, and we'll decide your final placement based on deal flow, team priorities and where you add the most. You'll do real day-to-day work supporting the team where it matters most. Workstreams include:

  • Sell-side execution: supporting our sell-side Transaction Managers across the deal lifecycle. Qualifying inbound and outbound vendor leads, preparing materials, populating Virtual Data Rooms, and coordinating buyer Q&A.

  • Buy-side execution: supporting our buy-side Transaction Manager managing the live pipeline of searchers and acquirers. Qualifying buyer mandates, matching them to live sell-side opportunities, and helping move deals through to LOI.

  • Due diligence support: working with our DD Manager on company valuation and diligence for live sell-side mandates. Turning raw SME data into clear reports on business model, financial position, and fair valuation.

  • Origination: identifying SMEs likely to sell, running our "likely seller" models against iwoca's customer base, and converting matches into mandates.

  • Product, data & AI: turning manual workflows into automated ones, mapping the data schema for our "Digital IM", and building AI-enabled tooling that gives our Transaction Managers leverage. You'll work closely with the Venture Lead on this.

Phase 2: The project (months 3-6). Once you've built the foundation, you'll scope a project with the Venture Lead to solve a real problem or seize an opportunity you've identified during Phase 1. You'll spend the rest of the internship executing it end-to-end with full ownership and regular check-ins. Examples of the kind of project we'd back: a model that scores acquisition targets against a buyer's mandate, an AI workflow that drafts a first-pass IM from raw accounts, or a structured outbound channel into a new vendor segment.

Who you are

You're interested in M&A, FinTech, or building things from scratch, and you want to do all three at once. Most importantly, you're smart, motivated, humble, and have a growth mindset.

  • You are need-driven. You take whatever is in front of you and move it forward, whether that's fixing a broken spreadsheet, calling a vendor, or cleaning up CRM data. You don't wait to be told what's important.

  • You are financially literate. You can read a P&L and a balance sheet, spot what's odd, and ask the question that surfaces the real story behind the numbers.

  • You are tech-curious. You bring your own stack, you're already using AI tools to multiply your output, and you treat any manual workflow you see as a candidate for automation.

  • You are a clear communicator. M&A runs on trust. You write professional emails, you're not afraid to pick up the phone, and you can hold a conversation with a business owner about the company they spent 30 years building.

The requirements

  • Available for a full-time, off-cycle placement of up to 6 months.

  • Strong academic background, open to all disciplines.

  • Any experience, projects, or initiatives that show genuine M&A, FinTech, or entrepreneurial interest. We care more about evidence of initiative than a polished CV.

  • Bonus: experience working with SME data, financing, or M&A workflows.

The salary & conversion

This is a paid internship with annual compensation of £30k. If it goes well and there's a fit on both sides, we'd convert you into a permanent role on the manda team, with compensation re-benchmarked against the new position.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Join the Tilt teamAt Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss.
jobs.description:
Join the Tilt team

At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.

The Opportunity: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, ML Platform

ML is core to what Tilt does: our models make credit decisions for millions of customers across multiple markets, and they run on a platform shared by several business units. You’ll own the layer between data science and infrastructure. Half your time goes to running our managed feature store, and the other half to building the training and deployment platforms that let data scientists ship without an engineer in the loop.

The foundation is in place: a feature store, standard pipelines and an automated deployment framework. The team is now moving quickly into deep learning and streaming models. You’ll own the platform layer that sits between data science and infrastructure, and your measure of success is how much faster and more independently data scientists can move because you built it. You’ll thrive here if you go find the pain points yourself, turn them into platform work, and stay with each project until data scientists are actually using it.

Tilt is remote-first. We come together in person at least twice a year for company offsites — and those gatherings are worth the trip.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Run our managed feature store: build the patterns and tooling for defining, backfilling, and serving features so a new model can be trained from existing features and deployed.

  • Make the feature store the starting point for model training, not just deployment, so new models are trained on existing features instead of rebuilt pipelines.

  • Build and improve our automated training and deployment platforms. Our ML engineers own frameworks, not individual models.

  • Turn the steps data scientists repeat (registering features, launching training jobs, promoting a model, setting up monitoring) into self-service agents and skills they run themselves.

  • Standardize training and retraining so refits are schedulable, reproducible and backed by feature store data rather than one-off queries.

  • Scale batch scoring and low-latency online inference, with autoscaling, resource isolation and cost controls that hold up as the number of models grows.

  • Extend monitoring for data drift, feature drift, prediction quality and serving health, with alerts and dashboards data scientists use without escalating to engineering.

  • Define standards for model and feature versioning, lineage, testing and documentation, and lead their adoption across data science teams.

Why You’re a Great Fit

  • Deep hands-on experience as a platform or software engineer working in ML, with a track record of platforms that served many models in production across multiple teams.

  • Experience with feature stores and model deployment platforms, such as Databricks Feature Store, Feast, Tecton or equivalent. Time on a managed feature store is especially relevant.

  • Strong CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines or similar), model registries, and infrastructure as code with Terraform.

  • Cloud expertise in AWS or Azure for ML deployment, plus Kubernetes, workflow orchestration, and a strong command of batch and real-time serving, autoscaling, and latency and cost trade-offs.

  • You’ve removed engineers from the deployment loop with self-service tooling that data scientists actually adopted, and you’ve worked side by side with backend engineers to get deployments live instead of handing models off.

  • You work well with ambiguity: you gather requirements from stakeholders without being directed, propose solutions and drive projects to completion.

  • Enough depth in model development and common algorithms to be a real technical partner to data scientists. Familiarity with PySpark, Databricks and monitoring tools such as Evidently AI is a plus.

Our Interview Process

  1. Initial Recruiter Call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you’re looking for in your next role.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper discussion about your experience.

  3. Skills Panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach.

  4. Leadership Conversation: A final conversation with a leader to discuss how you’ll contribute to Tilt’s mission, and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way.

Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.

What you'll get at Tilt

  • Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.

  • Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.

  • Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.

  • Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.

  • Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)

  • Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.

The Tilt Way

We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.

You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

Compensation Range: $220K - $265K

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

About the Role

We are looking for a People Operations Specialist - Regional to manage day-to-day HR operations for employees across multiple countries.

You will work across payroll, EOR and HR vendors, onboarding and offboarding, employee records, and local employment requirements. The role currently supports approximately 15-20 countries and will expand as BJAK grows into new markets.

What You Will Need

  • 2+ years of experience in HR operations, payroll, people operations or a related role.

  • Experience supporting employees across multiple countries is strongly preferred.

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when handling payroll, employee data and employment documentation.

  • Ability to research local employment requirements and turn them into clear processes and documentation.

jobs.title: Director of ERISA Compliance
jobs.excerpt: Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.
jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

The Director of Retirement Compliance is a strategic, high-impact leadership role responsible for ensuring that Human Interest’s platform operates with regulatory precision under ERISA, DOL, and IRS guidelines. This leader will drive continuous innovation across compliance workflows, architecting root-cause feedback loops to resolve plan errors and delinquencies while driving the end-to-end compliance health of our plans at scale.

Operating at the intersection of regulatory governance, incident management, and product delivery, the Director will oversee high-level customer advocacy escalations in close partnership with Legal, steer feature rollout reviews, and build real-time monitoring infrastructure for SLAs and regulatory deadlines. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Sales Activation & Customer Success, this individual will proactively manage risk and financial exposure, own remediation solutions end-to-end, and actively coach and uplevel frontline compliance managers.

About the team

The Compliance team serves as the guardian of Human Interest’s regulatory integrity and fiduciary excellence. We sit at the nexus of regulatory compliance, customer success, onboarding, operations, and product engineering. Rather than acting as a traditional back-office audit function, our team acts as proactive problem solvers—designing scalable automation, building data pipelines, and establishing closed-loop operational workflows that safeguard plan sponsors and participants. As we continue to democratize access to retirement benefits, we're looking for a visionary leader who can scale our compliance operations through technology while maintaining our commitment to fiduciary excellence.

What you get to do every day

  • Lead and direct Human Interest's compliance program ensuring adherence to ERISA, DOL, and IRS regulations across all 401(k) plan operations
  • Modernize compliance workflows and build cross-functional feedback loops with Customer Onboarding, Customer Success, and Product to perform root-cause analysis on errors and delinquencies.
  • Develop and implement technology-driven compliance frameworks that scale with our growing client base while maintaining regulatory excellence
  • Own and drive scalable, technology-enabled initiatives with Product to improve platform-wide plan compliance health.
  • Design and oversee automated compliance monitoring systems to proactively identify and address potential issues
  • Build and manage operational dashboards to continuously track team SLAs, operational metrics, and statutory regulatory deadlines.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Operations, and Technology teams to review platform feature rollout plans, system copy, and marketing collateral to guarantee strict alignment with ERISA and DOL standards.
  • Lead Customer Advocacy and incident management for high-level escalations in close partnership with Legal to resolve plan errors and mitigate exposure.
  • Oversee fiduciary governance processes and ensure proper documentation of fiduciary decisions
  • Lead compliance technology initiatives including plan document automation, testing workflows, and regulatory reporting systems
  • Manage relationships with external auditors, regulatory bodies, and compliance consultants
  • Drive continuous improvement of compliance processes through automation and process optimization
  • Advise executive leadership on compliance risks and operational failures, proposing and owning strategic remediation solutions end-to-end.as primary point of contact for regulatory inquiries and examinations
  • Develop and maintain compliance policies, procedures, and training programs
  • Lead crisis management protocols for compliance-related issues requiring immediate attention
  • Coach, mentor, and uplevel frontline compliance managers to build operational excellence and scale team leadership.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What you bring to the role

  • 10+ years of experience in ERISA compliance, with at least 5 years in leadership roles within retirement plan administration
  • Current ERISA-related professional certifications (QKA, QPA, RPF, or equivalent)
  • Proven track record of leveraging technology to drive compliance efficiency and scalability
  • Experience with 401(k) plan administration, including nondiscrimination testing, plan document maintenance, and fiduciary oversight
  • Strong ability to develop compliance frameworks and processes that drive measurable results
  • Experience implementing compliance technology solutions and automated testing systems
  • Exceptional communication skills with ability to translate complex regulatory requirements for diverse stakeholders
  • Data-driven approach to compliance management and risk assessment

Nice to have

  • Advanced ERISA certifications (CEBS, CPC,)
  • Juris Doctor (JD) with an emphasis on ERISA, employee benefits, or administrative law
  • Experience within a high-growth fintech, modern TPA, or SaaS retirement platform.
  • Track record of implementing compliance automation in high-growth environments
  • Experience scaling compliance functions from startup to enterprise stage
  • Background in regulatory technology (RegTech) or compliance software implementation
  • Proven ability to influence regulatory strategy based on industry trends and regulatory changes
  • Experience managing both remote and in-office compliance teams
  • Knowledge of emerging compliance technologies including AI and machine learning applications
  • Practical familiarity with workflow automation tools (e.g., Jira, Gemini) and dashboarding software (e.g., Salesforce, Hex).
  • Deep background navigating voluntary correction programs (IRS EPCRS and DOL VFCP/DFVCP).

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

  • Customer obsession: We're all about creating amazing experiences for our customers. We put their needs first and go the extra mile to make them smile.
  • Long-Term Orientation: We're not just playing for today; we're building a legacy. We think big, plan strategically, and invest in our future.
  • Autonomous and Accountable Teams: We trust our team members to take ownership and make smart decisions. We empower you to be your best self!
  • An Escalating Bar for Talent and Performance: We're constantly raising the bar and challenging ourselves to be better. We believe in growth and continuous improvement.
  • Fundamental Optimism: We see the glass as half full (and then we fill it up with more amazing ideas!). We believe in the power of positivity and the potential for greatness.

Compensation - At Human Interest, there are a number of factors that are used to determine the appropriate pay range for each position.   • Experience with account-based outbound strategies and modern prospecting tools

You don’t need to have worked in video communications before. What matters most is your ability to understand a technical product, identify meaningful business problems and create opportunities through thoughtful, targeted selling.

🌎 We believe in everyone

We fundamentally believe talent is distributed to all of us in equal measure. We open our doors (physical or URL) to everyone and we see our differences as a strength; it’s this philosophy that drives us towards our mission.

This means we see your unique history as having value money cannot buy; we believe in the strength of every intersection of race, religion or belief, ethnic origin, different physical ability, family structure, socio-economics, age, nationality, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity.

Help shape our commercial approach

Your progression

jobs.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role

Parachute Health is building the definitive platform for ordering home medical equipment and supplies, helping clinicians and suppliers ensure that millions of patients each year receive the critical equipment and supplies they need. Our Merchandising Operations team (AKA “Merch”) comprises Category Managers and Category Analysts who have three primary jobs: 1) build and maintain our catalog, 2) build and maintain our coverage criteria rules engine, and 3) partner with R&D to improve the tools and workflows behind both. Merch sits at the intersection of e-commerce, compliance, operations, and R&D, and its work is central to Parachute's core functionality. Clinicians use our catalog to find and order the right equipment for their patients, and suppliers rely on it to fulfill those orders. Our coverage criteria help users determine whether an item should be covered by the patient's insurance.

The Merch team's work is nuanced and detail-dense: we maintain information on tens of thousands of products so our software, and the people who use it, can rely on it. The 18-person team splits its time between project work, like building and redesigning product categories and turning payer rules into qualification questions, and ticket-based work, resolving complex requests escalated by our support and partner teams. Our work requires efficient operational processes and excellent documentation.

As Director of Merchandising Operations, you will own the team's operating framework: how work is planned, prioritized, and delivered, and how the team partners with other teams across Parachute. You'll coach and develop a mix of managers and individual contributors, lead the team's largest cross-functional projects, and serve as a close thought partner to the SVP of Merchandising.

The role is primarily internal (roughly 90%), with occasional customer communication, especially on escalations, that calls for a steady, polished hand.

What You'll Do

  • Be the operational leader for a highly motivated, highly capable team of managers and individual contributors: keep work running smoothly, protect morale, and learn and add to a team culture that is already strong.
  • Drive key projects: stay close to the work and personally drive the team's largest, most complex projects, including timelines, dependencies, and cross-team communication.
  • Know every team process end to end. Lead the creation, maintenance, and centralization of SOPs and shared resources; drive consistent practices, training, quality assurance, and continuous improvement across category teams.
  • Collaborate with partner teams (e.g., Supplier Implementation, Product, Customer Success) so handoffs and shared processes run smoothly.
  • Be a Merch advocate: make the team's work understandable and visible across the company.
  • Run bandwidth and capacity planning; flag risks early and rebalance coverage.
  • Define and report on team metrics (ticket throughput, SLAs, SKU work, rollout milestones).
  • Own escalations as needed, partnering effectively with people at all levels across the organization.
  • Support recruiting as needed, own onboarding for new merchants, and maintain continuity coverage for every category.

Requirements

  • 7+ years in operations, program delivery, or management or technology consulting (e.g., a Big Four or top-tier firm), with 3+ years managing and growing managers.
  • Track record of delivering complex, cross-functional projects using a clear, repeatable methodology.
  • Data-driven: comfortable with capacity models, dashboards and prioritization trade-offs.
  • Willingness to travel roughly once a quarter.

More About You

  • Passionate about improving patient outcomes in the healthcare space.
  • Gets things done: drives work to completion and builds processes that stick.
  • Thrives in complex, nuanced domains; quickly learns intricate systems (e.g., insurance coverage rules, product data) well enough to make sound calls.
  • Clear, concise communicator who pushes back constructively and drives decisions.
  • Sound compliance judgment: in a highly regulated industry, you know which issues to resolve and which to escalate.

jobs.excerpt: About RunwareRunware is the AI inference platform that builds and operates its own infrastructure, end to end.
jobs.description:
About Runware

Runware is the AI inference platform that builds and operates its own infrastructure, end to end. One API gives developers access to image, video, audio, 3D and language models, and our Sonic Inference Engine runs them on hardware we designed ourselves: custom servers, custom boards and a closed-loop, water-free cooling system, packed into Sonic Inference Pods — roughly 1 MW of liquid-cooled GPU compute in a 20-foot container that can be sited wherever power is cheap and available.

This is why infrastructure at Runware is the product, not a cost center. Our edge is that we run inference 30–90% cheaper per GPU-hour than our peers, and that edge is earned in the data center: in how fast we can stand up a new site, how tightly we run our fleet, and how little downtime our customers ever see. More than 20 billion requests have run through the platform for over a million developers, with customers such as Wix, Quora, Freepik and Higgsfield building production applications on top of it.

We raised a $50M Series A led by Dawn Capital, with Comcast Ventures, Speedinvest, Insight Partners and a16z speedrun participating, and we are now building out a global network of pods across the US and Europe. We need someone to own how that network is operated.

The Role

As Network Architect, you'll own the design, build, and operation of the network that moves every inference request through Runware: the GPU cluster fabric inside our data centers, the backbone and edge that deliver results to customers, and the cloud and hybrid connectivity that ties partner capacity into one platform. Runware's product is latency. The network is where a large share of that latency, and of our cost per request, is decided, and today there is no single owner for it. You'll be that owner.

This is a senior, hands-on architecture role with significant authority and no direct reports to start. You'll report to Risto Haukioja, Head of AI Infrastructure. You'll set the network strategy, design and build the systems yourself, define how they are operated and capacity-planned, and lead through design authority across Infrastructure, Platform, and ML Engineering. You've run high-performance teams before, and you'll shape the standards and hiring plan for network engineering as the footprint grows. We expect you to use AI tooling as a core part of how you work, so that one architect can produce what a small team used to.

What you'll do

  • Own the network architecture end to end. Define the target architecture and multi-year roadmap for Runware's data center fabric, backbone and edge, and cloud and hybrid connectivity, and make the design decisions that trade off latency, throughput, cost, and resilience.
  • Design and build the GPU cluster fabric. Architect spine-leaf fabrics for multi-node inference and training: 400G/800G Ethernet, RoCEv2 and InfiniBand, lossless transport, congestion control, and topology choices that keep east-west traffic from becoming the bottleneck.
  • Deliver inference to customers fast and reliably. Own the backbone and edge: multi-region interconnect, transit and peering strategy, anycast and traffic steering, DDoS and edge security posture, and the path that gets every response to the customer with as few milliseconds as possible.
  • Connect cloud, bare metal, and partner capacity into one platform. Design VPC, VPN, and private interconnect across hyperscalers, bare-metal providers, and colocation sites so new capacity can be brought online quickly and operated consistently.
  • Build network operations, not just networks. Define how the network is monitored, changed, and repaired: telemetry and observability, change management, incident runbooks, and on-call practices that hold up at scale. Stand up what doesn't exist yet.
  • Run capacity planning. Build the models that forecast bandwidth, port, and interconnect needs from product growth, and turn them into procurement and build plans with lead times that match the business, not the other way round.
  • Automate the network. Treat network configuration as code: IaC, intent-based provisioning, automated validation and rollback, and telemetry-driven remediation, so the network can grow without a proportional growth in people.
  • Accelerate your own output with AI. Use AI tools throughout your work (design exploration, configuration generation, log and telemetry analysis, documentation, automation code) and set the standard for how the wider infrastructure team does the same.
  • Lead through design authority. Set network standards, review designs across Infrastructure, Platform, and ML Engineering, mentor engineers, and define the hiring plan and operating model for network engineering as the footprint grows.
  • Own vendor and carrier relationships. Evaluate and select hardware, optics, carriers, and interconnect partners, and negotiate for performance and cost.

Requirements

  • 15+ years in network engineering and architecture, including at least 5 years as the design authority for large-scale production networks at a cloud provider, hyperscaler, CDN, HPC/AI infrastructure company, or carrier.
  • Hands-on. You still design, configure, and troubleshoot networks yourself, and you've built data center, backbone, and cloud networks from the ground up, not just inherited them.
  • Deep, current expertise in modern data center networking: spine-leaf Clos fabrics, EVPN/VXLAN, BGP at scale, 400G/800G Ethernet, RoCEv2 and lossless Ethernet (PFC, ECN, DCQCN), and InfiniBand for GPU clusters.
  • Strong backbone and edge experience: multi-region interconnect, transit and peering, anycast, traffic engineering, and DDoS mitigation, with a track record of measurably reducing customer-facing latency.
  • Cloud and hybrid networking across at least two hyperscalers plus bare-metal or colocation environments: VPC design, private interconnect (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect or equivalent), and VPN at scale.
  • Experience designing and running network operations: observability, change management, incident response, and on-call, with the judgement to know what to build first when starting from little.
  • Proven capacity planning: you've built forecasting models that turned product growth into bandwidth, port, and interconnect plans, and you've run the procurement cycles that followed.
  • Network automation as a working practice, not an aspiration: Python or Go, IaC for network config, CI-style validation, and streaming telemetry.
  • You use AI to accelerate your own output. You can show how AI tooling is part of how you design, write configuration and automation code, analyse telemetry, and document, and you expect it to multiply what you ship.
  • Experience leading high-performance engineering teams: you've hired, set standards, and run teams that delivered under pressure, and you lead well through influence when you have no direct reports.
  • Strong ownership and comfort in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where you identify the problems, create clarity, and drive the work to done.
  • Based in, or with full working overlap with, US Pacific time.

Strong Differentiators

  • Experience networking large GPU clusters for AI inference or training (NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Quantum InfiniBand, NCCL tuning, GPUDirect RDMA), and an opinion on Ethernet versus InfiniBand backed by production numbers.
  • Hands-on with modern network operating systems and disaggregated hardware: SONiC, Cumulus, Arista EOS, Junos, or NVIDIA Cumulus/Spectrum platforms.
  • Experience with Ultra Ethernet, 800G and 1.6T optics, co-packaged optics, or other emerging fabric technologies.
  • Experience running peering and transit for a latency-sensitive product, including ASN management, route optimisation, and IXP presence.
  • Experience with eBPF, DPDK, SmartNICs/DPUs, or kernel-bypass networking on the host side.
  • Prior work at a startup or scale-up where you built the network function from zero.
  • Public contributions: RFCs, open-source network tooling, conference talks, or published post-mortems.

Benefits

We're a remote-first collective, meeting in person twice a year to plan, brainstorm, celebrate wins, and enjoy some face-to-face time. We have core hours for cooperative working and calls, but outside of that your calendar is yours. Work the hours that let you perform at your peak while also building a healthy life.

Our release cycles are fast and intense, but they're followed by real downtime. After big pushes we expect the team to unplug, recharge, and come back ready and stronger than ever for the next leap.

  • Generous paid time off: vacation, sick days, public holidays
  • Meaningful stock options: share in the upside you create
  • Flexible hours: own your schedule outside core collaboration blocks
  • Family leave: paid maternity, paternity, and caregiver time
  • Company retreats: twice-yearly gatherings in inspiring locations
