$120,000-$160,000/salary



Job Description:

HRIS Lead - Workday

Point Quest Group | Job Description


Position Summary

The HRIS Lead - Workday owns the administration, configuration, security, and optimization of the Workday platform. This role serves as the technical subject matter expert and functional lead for HR technology, ensuring reliable system architecture, accurate reporting, training key stakeholders, strong data governance, and solutions that support business priorities.

This is a hands-on individual contributor position with no direct reports. The role requires deep Workday expertise, independent judgment, and close partnership with the HR Director, Workday Project Manager and IT.


Key Responsibilities

Workday System Administration and Architecture

  • Serve as the primary Workday administrator across HCM, Time Tracking, Benefits, Absence, and Recruiting; partner with Payroll on payroll-related configuration and issues.
  • Configure and maintain business processes, calculated fields, condition rules, notifications, and validations that support consistent and scalable workflows.
  • Apply knowledge of Workday architecture and data relationships to evaluate how configuration, process, and security changes affect connected modules, payroll, reports, integrations, and the employee experience.
  • Configure and troubleshoot complex Absence plans, eligibility rules, accruals, balances, and policy requirements in partnership with HR and Payroll.
  • Support Workday Recruiting configuration and workflows, including connections to hiring, onboarding, and employee records.
  • Maintain tenant configuration, configuration workbooks, system documentation, and change logs.

Security and Data Governance

  • Design and maintain role-based and user-based security groups, manage approved access provisioning and removal, and conduct periodic access reviews.
  • Configure domain security policies governing access to data and tasks, and business process security policies governing who can initiate, approve, review, and act on transactions.
  • Evaluate security changes for appropriate access, segregation of duties, confidentiality, and downstream effects; test and document approved changes before deployment.
  • Establish data quality standards, conduct audits, and coordinate corrections to protect the accuracy and integrity of HRIS data.
  • Support internal controls, applicable data privacy requirements, and internal and external audits; maintain access and security documentation.

Reporting and Analytics

  • Build and maintain custom, advanced, and composite Workday reports, dashboards, and reporting calculated fields for HR, Payroll, Finance, and business leaders.
  • Help stakeholders locate, interpret, and use Workday standard reports; translate business questions into reporting requirements.
  • Validate report accuracy, performance, and security, and support data extracts and downstream reporting needs.

Integrations and Vendor Connections

  • Manage and monitor Workday integrations and external vendor data connections, including API integrations, EIBs, Core Connectors, and Workday Studio integrations as applicable to the environment.
  • Partner with IT and vendors on integration design, testing, troubleshooting, and remediation; validate the accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of data flows.
  • Assess how changes to configuration, security, and business processes affect integrations and connected systems.

Production Support and Stabilization

  • Manage the Workday Support inbox, triage and prioritize requests based on business impact, track resolution, and communicate status and next steps to stakeholders.
  • Provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 production support, investigate root causes, and coordinate complex issue resolution with Workday Support, IT, vendors, and functional owners.
  • Collaborate closely with and support the Workday Project Manager during stabilization, including issue tracking, remediation, testing, and transition to ongoing operations.

Release Management and Strategic Planning

  • Lead release impact assessments, testing, and deployment planning, including unit testing, regression testing, and user acceptance testing.
  • Partner with functional leaders to develop and prioritize a Workday roadmap that aligns system capabilities, automation, and future enhancements with business needs.
  • Lead approved optimization initiatives and recommend feature adoption based on business value, readiness, and effects across the platform.
  • Support evaluation and, if approved, implementation of Workday Performance Management, including requirements, configuration, testing, and rollout.
  • Provide technical guidance, documentation, and training to HR and Payroll power users to improve system adoption and effective use.

Other Duties as Assigned

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, tasks, duties, or responsibilities required of this position. Duties, responsibilities, tasks, and activities are subject to change at any time with or without notice.


Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • At least five years of hands-on Workday administration experience supporting production environments.
  • Deep expertise in Workday business process configuration, calculated fields, advanced and composite reporting, dashboards, and security administration, including domain and business process security policies.
  • Strong understanding of Workday architecture and the dependencies among configuration, security, reporting, integrations, and business processes.
  • Hands-on experience supporting Workday Absence and Recruiting, including complex absence policies; foundational knowledge of Workday Payroll and its dependencies on time, absence, and employee data.
  • Experience supporting Workday integrations and troubleshooting data exchanges, including API integrations and relevant Workday integration tools.
  • Experience with tenant management, release assessments, testing, and controlled deployment of configuration changes.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently resolve complex issues and manage competing priorities as a senior individual contributor.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into practical system solutions, communicate technical concepts clearly, and collaborate effectively across corporate functions.
    •

Preferred

  • Relevant Workday certifications or completed Workday training in HCM, reporting, security, or integrations.
  • Experience with EIBs, Core Connectors, and Workday Studio; experience with Prism Analytics or Workday Extend.
  • Experience in multi-state, multi-entity environments with complex business structures.
  • Experience supporting Workday implementations, post-implementation stabilization, or major optimization projects.
  • Experience implementing or supporting Workday Performance Management.
  • Knowledge of SOX controls and audit support.

This position operates in a primarily remote professional environment, with occasional onsite or in-person meetings as business needs require. jobs.description:
Position Type: Full-Time | Remote

Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented Medical Billing Specialist to manage the end-to-end medical billing and claims process. In this role, you will be responsible for submitting accurate insurance claims, posting payments, investigating denials, and following up on outstanding accounts receivable.

You will work closely with the Finance team to ensure billing operations run smoothly, reimbursements are tracked accurately, and outstanding issues are resolved in a timely manner. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with medical billing workflows, a solid understanding of insurance requirements, and the ability to work independently in a remote environment.

What You’ll Own

Claims Submission & Management

  • Prepare, review, and submit medical claims to insurance payers.
  • Verify claim accuracy and ensure all required coding and supporting documentation are included.
  • Monitor claim status and address submission errors or rejections.

Payment Posting & Reconciliation

  • Post insurance payments, adjustments, and patient payments to the appropriate accounts.
  • Review Explanation of Benefits (EOBs) and Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA) for payment accuracy.
  • Identify and investigate discrepancies between expected and received reimbursements.

Denial Management & Appeals

  • Investigate denied and rejected claims to identify underlying issues.
  • Prepare and submit corrected claims or appeals within payer deadlines.
  • Track denial trends and help prevent recurring billing errors.

Accounts Receivable Follow-Up

  • Monitor outstanding claims and unpaid balances.
  • Follow up with insurance companies regarding delayed or missing payments.
  • Maintain accurate records of aging accounts and escalate unresolved issues when necessary.

Patient & Payer Communication

  • Respond to billing-related inquiries from patients and insurance representatives.
  • Resolve payment discrepancies and clarify claim-related questions.
  • Maintain professional and timely communication with external payers and internal stakeholders.

Compliance & Documentation

  • Follow applicable healthcare billing regulations, payer requirements, and internal procedures.
  • Maintain accurate billing records and protect confidential patient information.
  • Keep shared trackers and Finance team documentation updated.

Requirements

  • Proven experience in medical billing, claims processing, or a similar healthcare finance role.
  • Strong understanding of medical coding systems, including ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS.
  • Hands-on experience with insurance verification, EOBs, payment posting, and remittance processing.
  • Experience using medical billing software or practice management systems.
  • Understanding of the complete medical billing and claims lifecycle.
  • Strong knowledge of insurance claim follow-ups, denial management, and appeals.
  • Excellent attention to detail and strong organizational skills.
  • Proficient written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with insurance payers and internal teams.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple billing tasks in a remote environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with U.S. healthcare billing and insurance processes.
  • Familiarity with common clearinghouses and electronic claims submission workflows.
  • Experience managing accounts receivable aging reports and identifying reimbursement trends.
  • Previous experience supporting a remote Finance or Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) team.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You identify billing discrepancies early and take ownership of resolving them.
  • You are proactive with claim follow-ups and do not let outstanding items go unattended.
  • You can manage repetitive, detail-heavy tasks while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
  • You communicate clearly with internal teams and external insurance representatives.
  • You understand the importance of patient data confidentiality and handle sensitive information responsibly.
  • You are organized, self-motivated, and comfortable working with minimal supervision.

What Success Looks Like

  • Medical claims are submitted accurately and within required timelines.
  • Payments and adjustments are posted correctly, with discrepancies identified promptly.
  • Denied claims are investigated and resolved through timely corrections or appeals.
  • Outstanding accounts receivable are consistently monitored and followed up.
  • Billing records and shared trackers remain accurate and up to date.
  • The Finance team has clear visibility into billing progress, outstanding issues, and potential blockers.

Interview Process

  • Initial application review.
  • Client interview
  • Final selection and offer.

jobs.excerpt: What you'll doWe're looking for someone genuinely exceptional: not broadly experienced, but specifically excellent in a way you can name and prove.
jobs.description:
What you'll do

We're looking for someone genuinely exceptional: not broadly experienced, but specifically excellent in a way you can name and prove. This role is for a data engineer who can walk into a platform someone else built, work out what is actually wrong with it, and decide what to fix first.

You'll join a small, senior Data & Analytics team at a real estate investment firm that has built a sophisticated data platform on Snowflake, pulling together 40+ data sources. Your job is to stabilize the environment, make reporting reliable, and automate the manual work, so that people can focus on the investment and operating decisions that matter.

Your work will support three areas of the business:

  • Transactions: buy/sell decisions, commercial leasing, and valuation

  • Reporting and source of truth: benchmarks, fund and asset performance, and management reporting

  • Day-to-day decision making: giving teams faster, better access to the information they need to run the business

You'll work directly with the client's technical and business teams, assess whether the platform is as strong as it looks, and raise the standard around you through code review, documentation, and the willingness to push back when something isn't right.

What we’re looking for

Depth in data engineering is the starting point. Beyond that we’re looking at judgment: knowing which problem to solve first in an environment with a lot of moving parts, and being able to explain that choice to people who aren’t engineers. We also pay attention to how AI shows up in the way you work.

You must bring:

  • 5+ years in data engineering, with real ownership of a production platform rather than contributing to someone else’s

  • Hands-on Snowflake: warehouse sizing and cost management, MERGE patterns, streams and tasks, clustering

  • Experience diagnosing and fixing pipelines you didn’t write: slow queries, unexplained cost, silent data quality failures

  • Experience designing, implementing, and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines and data integration across many sources

  • Strong data modeling: stating and enforcing grain, clean layering from raw through staging to marts, handling corrections and late-arriving data

  • Advanced SQL, including window functions and query performance work

  • Experience with a transformation framework (dbt or equivalent) and an orchestrator (Airflow, Dagster, or similar)

  • A working relationship with AI that shows up in how you build, not just in the tools you’ve tried

  • Comfort owning work end to end: from design through deployment and support

  • A quality mindset: clean code, good documentation, thoughtful testing, and attention to data quality and lineage

  • Strong English communication, async collaboration skills, and a proactive approach to problems

  • The ability to understand the business behind the data, not just the ticket in front of you

Bonus points for asset management or commercial real estate experience, familiarity with systems such as Yardi, MRI, RealPage, Argus, VTS, or CoStar, building analytics-ready models for BI tools (Power BI in particular), AWS Glue or EMR alongside Snowflake, exposure to workflow automation tools (Power Automate, UiPath), and a track record of mentoring other engineers.

Why You'll Love Working Here

Real impact. You'll work on meaningful products that make a measurable difference.

An outstanding team. Talented, kind, hard working people who care about their craft and about each other. No egos. No politics.

Growth. You'll be supported in growing your craft, exploring new paths, and stepping into greater responsibility, at your own pace.

A culture of excellence. We care about doing the right thing for our clients, our team, and ourselves. No burnout. No crunch. Just high quality work, delivered sustainably.

Variety and stability. We're profitable, independent, and over two decades strong. Yet every project brings a fresh challenge. You'll never be bored here.

This Role Might Not Be for You

We want to respect your time by being clear about what this role isn't. You should skip this opportunity if:

  • You prefer well defined structure. If you gravitate toward a clear hierarchy and well defined roles and swim lanes, you may find our self-managed style challenging.

  • Distributed work isn't your thing. If you find async communication, design documentation, and being proactive without a manager nearby difficult, our setup won't suit you.

  • Inheriting an existing environment doesn't appeal. This role starts by stabilizing and improving a platform someone else built, with a lot of moving parts. If you only want greenfield projects, you'll find it frustrating.

  • Feedback doesn't excite you. We're obsessed with quality and believe in continuous improvement. That means feedback that's sometimes nitpicky. If refining work until it's excellent feels over the top, this won't be a fit.

  • Change makes you uncomfortable. Priorities shift and processes evolve. If ambiguity is uncomfortable, this may feel bumpy.

However, if this sounds like fuel, we'd love to talk.

How to Apply and What to Expect in the Interview Process

  1. Your work. Show us the work that reflects you at your best. We'll look at depth, the quality of your thinking, and the logic behind your choices.

  2. Lateral team fit. You'll speak with our Talent team about your career direction, your motivators, and our plans ahead.

  3. Work trial. You'll tackle a take-home challenge that mirrors what we actually do.

  4. Engineering deep dive. A collaborative session with our engineers.

  5. Project fit. An interview focused on prioritisation, collaboration across disciplines, and how you handle the messy middle.

About the Job

The Title IV Compliance Administrator plays a critical role in supporting the integrity and effectiveness of Christ-centered higher education by ensuring institutional adherence to academic and federal compliance standards, including requirements under 34 CFR § 668.22 (Treatment of Title IV Funds When a Student Withdraws) and the Higher Learning Commission's Federal Compliance Requirements. The Compliance Administrator leads the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of processes related to FW grade reporting, faculty training and accountability, and financial aid compliance, exercising independent judgment and discretion in the resolution of compliance matters of institutional significance. This position is fully remote and reports to the Director of Faculty Development.

With a strong focus on training and communication, the Title IV Compliance Administrator is responsible for the design and delivery of faculty training, creating targeted communications, and ensures consistent application of university policies. The role serves as a key liaison across departments – including Financial Aid, Registrar, and academic leadership – to ensure timely, accurate, and actionable reporting practices.

Leveraging advanced technical proficiency in enterprise systems (e.g., Salesforce, Brightspace, Colleague, Oracle) and emerging AI tools, the Title IV Compliance Administrator drives process innovation, automation, and data-informed decision-making. The position also produces executive-level reports and insights to support Deans and senior leadership, contributing to faculty performance management and continuous improvement initiatives.

This role requires a high level of professionalism, discretion, and emotional intelligence, particularly when addressing sensitive faculty matters and compliance concerns, while maintaining alignment with the University's mission to deliver transformative, Christ-centered education.

Job Location

Remote - must reside and work legally in the U.S. All work must be performed within the U.S.

About CCU

Colorado Christian University is the premier interdenominational Christian university in Colorado and the Rocky Mountain region, delivering world class education to thousands of students. The fully accredited, nonprofit University is located in Lakewood, Colorado, a suburb of Denver.

Colorado Christian University was founded in 1914 on two principles – grace and truth. CCU's scriptural foundation comes from John 1:17: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. (ESV)

CCU's mission is Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth.

A leader in higher education, the University has been consistently ranked in the top 2 percent of colleges and universities nationwide for its core curriculum by the American Council of Trustees and Alumni. CCU has had nine consecutive years of enrollment growth and has been named one of the five fastest-growing master's granting universities by The Chronicle of Higher Education.

CCU offers more than 200 degree program options for traditional and adult studies through its College of Undergraduate Studies and College of Adult and Graduate Studies. More than 9,000 students attend the University on the main campus, in regional centers throughout Colorado, and online.

Scripture states all Christians are called to serve Christ and to minister to others. Because Christians are individuals with different gifts and callings, we serve Christ in a variety of ministry vocations. CCU invites you to explore how you may use your calling and gifts at the University.

What is Most Appealing About Working at CCU?

  1. Faith-friendly: CCU's culture is unique to higher education. Where else can you pursue academic excellence, yet read the Holy Bible, pray with teammates and students at work, and work to impact our culture in support of Christian values?
  2. Convictionally Christian: As a university, we have an enduring commitment to Christ, His Kingdom, and the truth of God's Word.
  3. Live out your calling: We are a traditional evangelical university where you can invest your God-given talents and abilities alongside coworkers and teammates, while having a profound influence on students as they deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ.
  4. Equip students for Kingdom work: You can be a part of helping students discover their callings and preparing them for positions of significant leadership in the church, business, government, education, and other professions, as a key part of our University's Strategic Priorities.

We're Looking for Candidates Who:

  1. Advanced level proficiency in the use and innovation of Microsoft Office products, Salesforce, Brightspace, Colleague, and AI tools.
  2. Proficiency in the development of professional development and training materials using current and innovative software.
  3. Effective communication with high-level decision makers, high emotional intelligence, and business acumen.
  4. Executive-level report production and data analysis skills.
  5. Working knowledge of Title IV federal financial aid compliance requirements and Higher Learning Commission accreditation standards.
  6. Ability to translate compliance and operational requirements into technical specifications for a software development team, and to manage cross-departmental projects involving IT and senior leadership stakeholders.
  7. Professionalism and discretion on sensitive matters including the exercise of independent judgment on matters of institutional significance.

Key Job Duties

Mission Contribution

Contribute to CCU's mission: Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth. In this role, the Compliance Administrator contributes to the University's mission by contributing to the quality of Christ-centered higher education received by CCU students.

Training and Administration

  1. Ideates, develops, and maintains training materials supporting FW grade policies and institutional standards for academic honesty and integrity, consistent with HLC Criterion 2.
  2. Leads the development and delivery of FW policy training to faculty and other stakeholders, including Instructional Coaches, the Office of Student Success, Enrollment Counselors, Deans, and Program Directors; ensures required training is completed and policies are consistently implemented. Reports non-compliant faculty to appropriate CAGS offices.
  3. Responsible for the creation, coordination and distribution of all FW grade-related communications.
  4. Drives the creation and maintenance of FW grade records to support institutional recordkeeping and HLC Federal Compliance Requirements.

Financial Aid Reporting

  1. Responsible for reviewing and following up on FW grades, coordinating with relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate reporting and appropriate financial aid determinations.
  2. Develops and maintains the perpetual calendar of FW grade due dates ensuring software programming, workflows, and communications plans are executed in a timely manner.
  3. Obtains and maintains relevant knowledge on federal aid compliance requirements.
  4. Liaise between the Office of Student Success, Registrar, Financial Aid, IT, individual faculty, and the CAGS Faculty Development Office to ensure timely and accurate reporting consistent with HLC's Federal Compliance Requirements governing Title IV program responsibilities.

Project Management

  1. Leads the investigation, development, and implementation of technology solutions to automate and improve the FW grade reporting process, including requirements definition, project management, and cross-functional coordination.
  2. Manages the evaluation and improvement of the FW reporting process, including the development and implementation of AI solutions.
  3. Develops executive-level reports on faculty performance and compliance and collaborates with relevant stakeholders to support institutional effectiveness and faculty development.

While performing the duties of this job, you may be required to walk, stand, sit, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, speak with clarity, and have appropriate vision and hearing capabilities. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. The employee may be required to work occasional irregular hours, including some nights and weekends. Colorado Christian University expects all faculty and staff to become a part of the University community by participating in activities and events that occur on the campus throughout the year, which may occur during evenings and weekends.

We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

Senior Product Designer, Knowledge Graph

This is a remote position based in Sweden.

The Opportunity:

As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success.

As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. This gives engineers, SREs, and their agents an up to date picture of their systems. We want anyone to be able to understand a system and resolve an incident faster, without writing queries or maintaining alert rules, not just the one person who happens to know it best.

Over time, you will develop deep expertise in your product area and associated customer and user personas, use cases, and workflows, which will enable you to design tailored, role-driven experiences.

You will also have an opportunity to contribute to the evolution of the Product Design team at Grafana by coaching and mentoring other designers, collaborating on team internal initiatives, and helping evolve new ways of working, learning, and having fun together as the team scales.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Enabling customers to easily understand and explore how their systems connect to each other. Find clear, simple ways to show complex, constantly-changing information without overwhelming the user
  • Translate research and data to experiences that are easy to digest and break down complexity
  • Tailor the experience to different target audiences, covering multiple user perspectives
  • Work cross-functionally with peers and leaders in engineering, product management, technical writing, and GTM functions, as well as other members of the Product Design team
  • Prioritise for delivering impact while balancing business priorities, customer wishes and technical considerations
  • Document user needs and pain points, design directions, UX trade-offs, and detailed designs for specific features and enhancements
  • Execute research and contribute to quantitative and qualitative research initiatives with researchers, cross-functional collaborators, customers, and members of the Grafana user community

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • 7+ years of relevant design experience working on B2B/enterprise software products, ideally designing tools and services for developers or other highly technical users
  • A portfolio of effective designs for complex products delivered in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience running qualitative research in complex fields, building empathy with users and humans, their needs and pain points even when you have very little in common with them
  • Ability to make design decisions that appropriately balance business goals, product priorities, customer feedback, research insights, and technical considerations
  • Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams across multiple locations and time-zones to iteratively ship and evolve products while keeping the end design vision in mind
  • Attention to detail and willingness to learn about a complex, very technical product space
  • Experience working in a fully-remote, fast-paced environment where you are expected to share openly, default to transparency, and embrace your autonomy

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience designing complex, data-dense interfaces with a focus on clarity
  • Ability to rapidly gain an understanding of a technical domain and associated customer needs and user workflows in order to design effective experiences within that domain
  • Domain knowledge or experience related to observability, cloud infrastructure, and/or database monitoring
  • Experience helping design teams, especially at engineering led companies, level up their practice, collaboration with partner functions, and user and organizational impact

When you apply, please:

  • Provide an example of an experience where decision-making in a complex area is made easy through a well-curated UI. Add a sentence or two about what you believe makes it effective.

Compensation & Rewards:

In Sweden, the Base compensation range for this role is SEK 721,312 - SEK 865,574. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

.

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Compliance Operations Specialist

About the job

This role is part of Twilio’s Compliance Operations team, which helps ensure that customer activity on our platform follows industry rules and Twilio’s internal policies. You’ll be responsible for reviewing alerts and account activity for Messaging and Voice traffic to assess whether it complies with Twilio’s Voice Policy, Messaging Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, and relevant regulatory requirements across global carrier networks.

When non-compliant activity is identified, such as messaging that violates local telecom rules or improper use of voice services, you’ll work with customers to explain the issue and guide them toward a compliant solution. In some cases, you’ll also take enforcement action to stop the non-compliant activity from continuing on Twilio’s platform.

This is an analytical and communication-heavy role that requires strong judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to work through ambiguous situations. You’ll be expected to make informed decisions and explain those decisions clearly to customers, even when the guidance may not always be black and white.

We’re looking for someone who enjoys digging into complex issues, learning how global telecom regulations apply to real-world traffic, and helping customers understand how to stay compliant. The ideal candidate is curious, investigative by nature, and comfortable with both independent research and customer-facing communication.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Investigate potential violations: Review account activity, messaging behavior, and data to identify signs of abuse or misuse. You'll be trained to spot red flags and patterns linked to spam or scams, and take quick action to mitigate risk.
  • Stop bad actors before they cause harm: You'll use internal tools and available data to find and shut down non-compliant activity that could negatively impact Twilio’s customers or consumers who receive unwanted calls or texts.
  • Communicate directly with customers: A major part of the job is customer-facing, primarily through email via our ticketing platform Zendesk. You'll notify customers of policy violations, provide them with clear guidance on how to fix issues, and sometimes inform them that their access to Twilio is being restricted or terminated.
  • Analyze trends and prevent future abuse: Go beyond individual cases by recognizing recurring themes, identifying root causes, and helping recommend long-term solutions to keep bad actors off the platform.
  • Work with data: You’ll regularly examine call and messaging records to trace activity, identify patterns, and support enforcement decisions with evidence.
  • Support global impact: The work you do directly affects businesses, mobile carriers, and end users around the world. Your decisions may impact high-profile brands and millions of consumers globally.
  • Prioritize clarity and accuracy: Because most communication is written, especially through email, you’ll need strong writing skills to explain policy violations and technical details in a way that customers understand and can act on.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • Willingness to work a non-traditional schedule; weekends, holidays and evenings may be required
  • Experience working in a fast paced, ambiguous environment, with a strong bias for action
  • You’re empathetic and love working with customers and carriers to solve their problems and questions, backed with data
  • You are detail-oriented with good organizational skills and comfortable with ambiguity
  • You have above average written and verbal communication skills and are able to articulate concepts/ideas in a clear, concise manner
  • You are willing to collaborate with communications partners and players in the industry to resolve issues, troubleshoot, and build trust
  • You have the ability to make sound decisions in a fast paced environment
  • You have good time management and organizational skills and are comfortable working under pressure
  • Excellent written communication skills in English

Desired:

  • Basic knowledge of using spreadsheets including formulas.
  • Have 1-2 years experience in fraud, abuse or compliance in ecommerce, FinTech, or telecommunications.
  • 1-2 years experience working in a queue based environment triaging and resolving tickets.

Location

This role will be remote, and based in Colombia.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

.

We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

jobs.description:
Acronis is a global leader in cyber protection, delivering AI-powered protection for productive MSPs in a single, natively integrated platform that unifies operations management, cybersecurity, and data protection. Driven by our mission to protect, manage and automate every workload that businesses and lives depend on, we’ve built the industry’s only all-in-one solution.

We are looking for an experienced Cyber Defense Unit Manager to lead and strengthen our global cyber defense capabilities. This role owns security operations, threat detection, incident response, threat intelligence, and proactive defense. You will build a high-performing team and continuously improve our ability to anticipate, detect, and respond to evolving cyber threats.

The ideal candidate combines deep cybersecurity expertise, operational leadership, and people management to build a modern, intelligence-driven cyber defense function. You are comfortable operating in a fast-paced global technology environment and can move seamlessly between strategy, hands-on operations, major incidents, and executive-level communication.

WHAT YOU’LL DO


Strategy and Leadership

  • Lead the Cyber Defense function, including strategy, roadmap, operating model, and continuous maturity improvement (e.g., against NIST CSF or SOC-CMM)
  • Manage, mentor, and develop a global team of analysts, responders, threat hunters, and detection engineers, ensuring coverage across time zones, including follow-the-sun or on-call models
  • Define the build-versus-buy approach for the function, including management of MDR/MSSP and other external partners, and manage the Cyber Defense budget

Security Operations, Monitoring, and Threat Hunting

  • Oversee 24x7 security monitoring, alert triage, investigation, and escalation across endpoints, networks, identities, applications, and cloud environments
  • Establish and maintain SOC processes, runbooks, severity definitions, and handoffs to ensure consistent, high-quality investigations
  • Lead proactive, hypothesis-driven threat hunting and attack surface monitoring, including identity-based and cloud-native threats

Detection Engineering

  • Own the detection engineering lifecycle: use case development, testing, tuning, deployment, and retirement, with a focus on reducing false positives and alert fatigue
  • Map detection coverage to MITRE ATT&CK, identify gaps, and prioritize improvements based on threat relevance and business risk
  • Ensure telemetry completeness by defining log source requirements and onboarding priorities with IT, Cloud, and Engineering
  • Run purple team and adversary emulation exercises to validate detection and response effectiveness

Incident Response

  • Lead response to significant cybersecurity incidents, coordinating across Security, IT, Engineering, Legal, Communications, and executive leadership
  • Maintain and test incident response plans, playbooks, and crisis communication procedures, including regular tabletop exercises with senior stakeholders
  • Oversee digital forensics, evidence handling, containment, eradication, and recovery, working with Legal to preserve privilege and support investigations, legal holds, and regulatory inquiries
  • Support breach assessment and regulatory notification decisions with Legal and Compliance (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, SEC disclosure, and other applicable obligations)
  • Run post-incident reviews and drive corrective actions to closure.

Threat Intelligence

  • Build and manage a threat intelligence capability that tracks threat actors, campaigns, and techniques relevant to Acronis, its customers, and the MSP ecosystem
  • Translate intelligence into actionable detections, hunts, blocking actions, and risk-informed recommendations for leadership
  • Participate in industry intelligence-sharing communities and partnerships (e.g., ISACs, peer groups, law enforcement liaison)

Technology, Automation, and AI

  • Own and optimize core cyber defense technologies, including SIEM, EDR/XDR, SOAR, and threat intelligence platforms, including roadmap, integrations, and vendor performance
  • Drive automation and AI-assisted capabilities to improve detection, enrichment, triage, investigation, and response, with appropriate governance and human oversight
  • Leverage Acronis’ own products and platform capabilities where appropriate to strengthen internal defense

Metrics, Reporting, and Executive Communication

  • Establish KPIs and reporting for cyber defense effectiveness, such as MTTD, MTTR, detection coverage, alert quality, incident trends, and threat exposure
  • Report cyber defense posture, major incidents, and risk trends to senior leadership, and when needed the Board and Audit Committee

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with Security leadership, IT, Cloud, Engineering, Product Security, and Legal to strengthen the company’s overall security posture
  • Coordinate with Vulnerability Management and Product Security on exploitable risks, emergency patching, and threat-informed prioritization
  • Support audits, customer assurance requests, and regulatory requirements related to monitoring and incident response

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Significant cybersecurity experience (typically 10+ years) in security operations, incident response, threat detection, or cyber defense, including 5+ years leading teams
  • Proven experience leading cybersecurity teams within a global technology or software environment, including distributed, multi-time-zone teams
  • Demonstrated experience leading major incident response efforts from detection through recovery and post-incident review
  • Strong understanding of modern attacker techniques, threat actor tradecraft, and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK
  • Hands-on knowledge of SIEM, EDR/XDR, SOAR, threat intelligence, and security monitoring technologies, including evaluation and optimization
  • Experience with threat hunting and detection engineering, including detection-as-code practices
  • Strong understanding of AWS, Azure, or other modern cloud environments, including cloud-native logging, detection, and response
  • Experience with digital forensics and investigations, and working knowledge of breach notification and regulatory requirements
  • Experience leveraging automation, scripting (e.g., Python), and ideally AI within security operations
  • Experience managing budgets, vendors, and managed security service providers
  • Strong leadership, analytical, and decision-making skills, particularly during high-pressure incidents
  • Ability to communicate complex cybersecurity risks clearly to technical and executive stakeholders, including legal and board audiences
  • High integrity and sound judgment when handling sensitive, confidential, and privileged information
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GIAC (GCIH, GCFA, GCTI, GCDA), or OSCP are a plus

WHO WE ARE

A Swiss company founded in Singapore in 2003, Acronis offers over twenty years of innovation with 15 offices worldwide and employees in 50+ countries. Acronis Cyber Protect is available in 26 languages in 150 countries and is used by over 21,000 service providers to protect more than 750,000 businesses.


Our corporate culture centers on innovation, accountability, and impact. We encourage our people to think boldly, challenge conventional approaches, and take ownership of outcomes. As a member of our global “A-Team,” you’ll operate in a high-growth, fast-paced environment where resilience, adaptability, and a commitment to continuous improvement drive success.


OUR INTERVIEW PRACTICES

To maintain a fair and genuine hiring process, we kindly ask that all candidates participate in interviews without the assistance of AI tools or external prompts. Our interview process is designed to assess your individual skills, experiences, and communication style. We value authenticity and want to ensure we’re getting to know you—not a digital assistant. To help maintain this integrity, we ask to remove virtual backgrounds and include in-person interviews in our hiring process.

Use of AI-generated responses or third-party support during live interviews may be grounds for disqualification from the recruitment process and a full criminal, education and identification background check is required for all new hires.

Acronis is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, color, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, medical condition, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.


The US pay range for this position is $170,000–$260,000. This range reflects the minimum and maximum total target annual compensation for this role across all U.S. locations. The actual compensation offered at the start of employment is determined based on factors including, but not limited to, experience level, knowledge, skills, and geographic location.

In addition to competitive compensation, this role includes a comprehensive benefits package featuring medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible spending accounts (FSA), disability and life insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and a generous vacation policy.

jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Remote, United States.  Up to 25% travel.  About the RoleWhen an ATS, staffing CRM, or industry software company partners with Onboarded, signing is the starting line.
jobs.description:
Remote, United States. Up to 25% travel.

About the Role

When an ATS, staffing CRM, or industry software company partners with Onboarded, signing is the starting line. From there, the partner's teams need to learn to sell and launch us, the first customers need to go live, and product gaps need to close fast enough that momentum holds once we step back. We're looking for someone to own that work end to end, bringing dedicated focus to turning each signed partnership into live customers and a growing book of business.

You'll own up to three partner ecosystems from signing to steady state. Sales opens the ecosystem and closes the partnership. Sometimes our engineers build what the partnership needs, and sometimes the partner's engineers build it on top of Onboarded. Customer Engineering supports partners and their customers once they're live. You sit in the middle as the architect and success owner for each ecosystem, accountable for how fast partner customers go live and how much of the work the partner can run on its own. You will operate autonomously and answer for the results.

Onboarded is the onboarding and compliance engine for high-volume and complex hiring. The platforms that serve staffing firms and employers are a core part of how we grow, because one partnership can bring us many customers. Deployment Strategist is a new role here, and the first people in the seat will write the playbook for how we grow every ecosystem we sign.

We're casting a wide net. Maybe you've held this title at an AI or data company. Maybe you've grown a partner channel, run solutions for an integration program, led implementations at a software company, or founded something. What matters is that you think like a product owner, can design how systems fit together, earn trust with engineers and partner executives alike, and use AI as a force multiplier.

What You'll Do

  • Own each ecosystem from signing to steady state. Join partnership deals before they close to plan who sells, implements, and supports. After signing, you drive partner customers live, ecosystem ARR, and the share of implementations the partner runs without us.
  • Teach partners to sell, launch, and support Onboarded. Train the partner's sales, customer success, and implementation teams, and build the enablement kits and launch playbooks they rely on. Work with Customer Engineering to get the partner's front-line support certified.
  • Launch the first partner customers, then make yourself unnecessary. Stay close on early go-lives, find what breaks, and turn every fix into a repeatable step. Each launch should make the next one faster and need less of you. Once the partner runs most implementations on its own, you hand the ecosystem to Customer Engineering and move to the next one.
  • Architect how each partnership fits together. Decide what gets built, why, and who builds it: our engineers, the partner's, or both. Design the integration with the partner's engineering team, including how their product calls Onboarded's REST API and MCP surfaces, how data moves between systems, and where each step of the workflow lives. Review their design before they build, and catch what will break at scale.
  • Turn partner requests into clear specs. Write the requirements and user stories that tell any engineer, ours or theirs, what they're building, for which customers, and how it fits Onboarded's broader product. Prioritize hard, and be the first person to test what ships.
  • Keep a written point of view on every ecosystem. At any moment you can answer who the ideal customer is, why the partner's customers aren't using us yet, and whether the gap is awareness, positioning, product fit, integrations, implementation, or pricing. You know the biggest constraint today and what it takes to reach the next phase, and you recommend whether we invest more, hold steady, or stop.

What We're Looking For

  • A product thinker first. You can take "we just have to have it" from a partner, figure out what they actually need, and come back with a crisp requirement or a clear no. You care more about building the right thing than saying yes to the next ask.
  • Experience growing something other people sell. 4+ years in partner solutions, solutions architecture, solutions engineering, product, or implementation leadership at a software company, or 2+ years in a builder or founder seat at a startup. You've enabled a channel, launched an integration program, or grown adoption inside someone else's customer base.
  • AI-first operator. You use AI tools as a force multiplier for enablement content, requirements, adoption analysis, prototyping, and everything in between. This is non-negotiable.
  • Real solution architecture skills. You can design an integration end to end: APIs, webhooks, authentication, data models, and how records stay in sync across systems. You've sat across from another company's engineering team, walked them through how to build on a product, and reviewed their design with a critical eye. You don't need to write production code, but you do need to whiteboard the system and spot the failure points before anyone builds. Experience as a solutions or partner architect is a strong signal.
  • A teacher who measures by what others can do. You've trained another company's sales or implementation team and know the difference between a great training session and a team that can run it without you.
  • Comfortable in every room. You can hold a strategy conversation with a partner's product and partnerships leaders in the morning, then work through a stuck launch with their implementation team in the afternoon.
  • Experience in staffing, ATS or HRIS software, or employment compliance (I-9, E-Verify, background checks, tax forms) is a strong signal but not required. Learning velocity and an AI-first approach to closing the gap count just as much.

This role is not a fit for someone who wants a support queue to work through or a pure quota-carrying sales seat. It is for builders who want to own an outcome, shape their own week around it, and leave every ecosystem able to grow without them.

Why This Role

  • You will own a number, not a queue. Your week starts with what your ecosystems need to grow. Your scoreboard is customers live and ecosystem revenue, and you decide how to move it.
  • You will write the playbook for a new role. You'll shape how Onboarded grows every partnership we sign, with a direct line to our founders, Product, Engineering, and partner executives.
  • There is a clear growth path. As we add ecosystems, this role can grow into leading a team of Deployment Strategists, owning ecosystem strategy, or moving into product leadership.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and equity in a fast-growing startup, plus variable pay tied to the growth of the ecosystems you own
  • Health, dental, vision, and retirement benefits
  • Remote-first culture with optional in-person collaboration
  • A chance to build the motion that grows every partner ecosystem we sign

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

We are seeking a Senior Lead Technical Marketing Manager to shape how Lumen brings its cybersecurity capabilities to market. This role translates complex security technologies, architectures, and threat intelligence into credible technical narratives, demonstrable solutions, seller-ready guidance, and customer experiences that accelerate adoption and revenue.

As a senior individual contributor, you will consult on and lead initiatives in partnership with many functions—Product Marketing, Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Partners, and our threat research team, Black Lotus Labs. You will own high-impact technical marketing programs across the cybersecurity portfolio and influence product and go-to-market decisions through customer insight, market evidence, technical depth, and commercial judgment.

Location and Schedule

This is a work-from-home position in the United States. Occasional travel is expected for customer engagements, industry events, demonstrations, sales enablement, and team planning sessions.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Own the technical marketing strategy: Define and execute technical marketing priorities for Lumen cybersecurity solutions, connecting portfolio strategy to customer use cases, architectures, adoption motions, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Create differentiated technical positioning: Develop clear, defensible messaging and value propositions for technical buyers and practitioners, including CISOs, security architects, SOC leaders, network leaders, and cloud security teams.
  • Build solution narratives and architectures: Translate cybersecurity capabilities into end-to-end reference architectures, validated use cases, solution blueprints, integration patterns, and deployment guidance across network, cloud, edge, and security operations environments.
  • Demonstrate the technology: Design and deliver compelling product demonstrations, technical workshops, webinars, videos, labs, and proof-of-value experiences that show how Lumen and its partners solve priority customer problems.
  • Lead technical content development: Create and govern high-value assets such as white papers, technical briefs, solution guides, blogs, FAQs, architecture diagrams, competitive guides, and technical launch materials.
  • Enable sellers and technical teams: Develop role-based training, discovery guidance, objection handling, battlecards, demo scripts, technical FAQs, and field playbooks that improve seller confidence, solution quality, and conversion.
  • Launch and support growth motions: Serve as the technical marketing lead for attach, cross-sell, and expansion motions. Ensure product, marketing, sales, and partner readiness before market activation.
  • Bring market and customer insight into decisions: Use customer conversations, competitive intelligence, analyst research, win-loss findings, field feedback, and performance data to identify gaps and recommend changes to product strategy, positioning, packaging, and activation.
  • Advance partner-led solutions: Collaborate with strategic cybersecurity partners to create integrated technical narratives, validated architectures, joint demonstrations, content, enablement, and go-to-market programs.
  • Represent Lumen as a technical authority: Engage customers, analysts, partners, and industry audiences as a cybersecurity subject-matter expert while maintaining accurate, evidence-based, and brand-safe claims.
  • Drive cross-functional execution: Lead complex workstreams without direct authority, establish clear outcomes and ownership, resolve dependencies, and create repeatable methods that improve the quality and speed of technical marketing execution.
  • Measure and optimize impact: Define success metrics and use adoption, pipeline, content, enablement, demonstration, and customer-feedback data to improve programs and prioritize investment.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, engineering, marketing, business or a related field, or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree or relevant security certifications are a plus.
  • 8+ years of experience in technical marketing, product marketing, product management, solutions engineering, technical pre-sales, cybersecurity consulting, or a related role.
  • Demonstrated cybersecurity depth across several domains such as network security, DDoS mitigation, SASE/SSE, firewalls, cloud security, threat intelligence, or security operations (SIEM/XDR/MDR).
  • Strong understanding of enterprise networking, cloud and hybrid architectures, security controls, telemetry, APIs, integrations, and operational workflows.
  • Proven ability to convert complex technical capabilities into clear customer value, differentiated positioning, credible proof points, and actionable field guidance.
  • Experience creating technical demonstrations, reference architectures, workshops, white papers, solution guides, or comparable practitioner-focused content.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively from hands-on practitioners through executive audiences.
  • Ability to lead complex, ambiguous initiatives across multiple functions without direct authority, while maintaining clear decisions, accountability, and momentum.
  • Commercial and analytical judgment, including the ability to connect technical marketing investments to adoption, pipeline, revenue, attach, retention, or expansion outcomes.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment with multiple priorities, high visibility, and a strong expectation for quality and execution.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience marketing managed security, network-embedded security, threat intelligence, or integrated networking and cybersecurity solutions.
  • Experience working with global telecommunications, cloud, networking, or managed security providers and their technology ecosystems.
  • Hands-on familiarity with security platforms, product labs, demonstration environments, scripting, APIs, or data visualization.
  • Established credibility with customers, analysts, technical communities, or industry events through presentations, publications, workshops, or thought leadership.

jobs.excerpt: Position: Technical Relationship Manager-Healthcare Location:United States – Remote Industry Focus:Healthcare (Health Systems, Hospitals, and Healthcare Delivery Organizations) THE ROLE: As a Technical Relationship Manager (TRM) on our Healthcare team, you'll be the main technical contact for a group of IGEL's health system and hospital customers.
jobs.description:
Position: Technical Relationship Manager-Healthcare
Location:United States – Remote 
Industry Focus:Healthcare (Health Systems, Hospitals, and Healthcare Delivery Organizations) 

THE ROLE:
As a Technical Relationship Manager (TRM) on our Healthcare team, you'll be the main technical contact for a group of IGEL's health system and hospital customers. You'll help them get more out of IGEL, from day-to-day issues to long-term planning. You'll work with our Technical Support, Product Management, Customer Success, and Renewals teams to get them what they need. 
This is a hands-on technical role combined with relationship management. Our customers run 24x7 clinical environments where endpoint uptime, fast and secure clinical application access, and protection of patient data directly affect patient care. Therefore, you'll need to understand both the technology and how clinicians use it. 

Travel Requirement: Up to 40% (customer sites, onsite technical reviews, and training) 

EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 5 years in a customer-facing enterprise role such as Technical Relationship Manager, Technical Account Manager, or similar.
  • At least 5 years of experience in engineering, consulting, system integration, or enterprise IT infrastructure with a technology vendor or reseller.
  • Experience in application and desktop virtualization, including Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, Omnissa Horizon (formerly VMware Horizon), or Microsoft Remote Desktop Services (AVD and Windows 365).
  • At least 2 years of hands-on experience with IGEL or similar enterprise technologies. IGEL experience is a big plus but not a must; strong technical and troubleshooting skills and a quick learning curve matter more.
  • Comfortable troubleshooting Windows and Linux systems and gathering diagnostic logs.
  • Clear communicator who builds strong customer relationships, stays organized, and maintains thorough documentation.
  • Self-directed, able to balance several customers and priorities at once, and experienced in running complex technical escalations.
  • Adapts easily to new technology, shifting customer needs, and large, complex IT environments.

Healthcare Experience – Strongly Preferred
  • Experience in healthcare organizations: integrated delivery networks, acute care hospitals, academic medical centers, ambulatory clinics, physician groups, long-term care, or payers.
  • Proven track record of working in large health systems running thousands of shared endpoints across hospitals, clinics, and data centers, from nursing stations and workstations on wheels (WOWs) to patient rooms.
  • Understanding of how EHRs like Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), and MEDITECH reach the endpoint, including how Epic Hyperspace/Hyperdrive is delivered through Citrix or Omnissa Horizon and how EHR upgrades and go-lives affect endpoints.
  • Hands-on knowledge of Imprivata and how clinicians share devices day to day.
  • Experience with clinical peripherals: badge readers, barcode scanners, label and wristband printers, signature pads, dictation devices (e.g., Nuance PowerMic/Dragon Medical), webcams, and headsets for telehealth.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA and one or more of the following: HITECH, PHI/ePHI safeguards, HITRUST CSF, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, audits, and access controls.
  • Exposure to Zero Trust, endpoint security, MFA (including EPCS), certificate-based authentication, network access control, and identity management.
  • Experience supporting around-the-clock clinical operations: downtime procedures, business continuity, disaster recovery, and getting endpoints back after ransomware or other cyberattacks.
  • Proven track record of leading urgent incidents that involve infrastructure, cybersecurity, networking, EUC, EHR application teams, and outside vendors.
  • Familiarity with how change works in healthcare: approval boards, clinical change windows, EHR upgrade cycles, freezes, risk assessments, and phased rollouts with at-the-elbow support.
  • Experience with Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), Windows 365, hybrid cloud, and optimizing Microsoft Teams for virtual care.
  • Experience conducting meetings with CIOs, CISOs, infrastructure and EUC leaders, CMIOs/CNIOs, and other technical decision-makers.

Nice to Have 
  • PowerShell, Bash, or Python scripting.
  • Experience with Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, or PostgreSQL.
  • Splunk, Grafana, or other monitoring tools.
  • ServiceNow or another ITSM platform.
  • Certifications like VCP, Citrix CCA/CCP, Microsoft, or networking and security credentials. Epic technical certifications (e.g., Epic Client Systems), CHPS, or HCISPP would be a strong plus.
  • Experience coordinating teams across time zones.

TASK AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop lasting partnerships with each customer's engineering, EUC, infrastructure, and clinical informatics teams and their leaders.
  • Understand how the customer's environment is built, how clinicians work, and what the organization is trying to achieve, and then act as their go-to technical advisor.
  • Share IGEL product knowledge and best practices that fit both clinical and non-clinical environments.
  • Help shape customers' end-user computing (EUC) direction and their Imprivata clinical workflows on IGEL, covering badge tap-in/tap-out, fast user switching, session roaming, and single sign-on.
  • Provide technical guidance on customer projects such as architecture changes, infrastructure modernization, EHR-driven endpoint updates, upgrades, migrations, and new rollouts.
  • Keep a technical account plan for each customer that captures their environment, clinical and business goals, dependencies, risks, and roadmap.
  • Lead regular account reviews covering IGEL platform health, open issues, planned upgrades, and risks, and suggest ways to improve performance, stability, security, and the clinician login experience.
  • Own support escalations with IGEL Support and Product Management until they're resolved. Help customers put forward enhancement and feature requests.
  • When critical incidents or downtime hit, pull in the right IGEL resources and keep the customer informed until service is restored.
  • Partner with Sales, Solutions Architects, and Renewals to spot where customers could expand their use of IGEL.
  • Coordinate and conduct customer meetings and onsite technical reviews with leadership.

WE OFFER

  • Health, dental, vision, and prescription benefits (employee premiums covered by IGEL)
  • 11 company-paid holidays per year
  • 18-22 days of PTO per year (18 days in year 1, 20 days starting in year 2 and 22 days after 5 years of service)
  • Sick time of 10 days per year, with rollover of unused days up to maximum limit
  • 401(k) plan with 100% company match, up to $15,000 per year
  • Paid maternity and paternity leave
  • Monthly home office allowance
  • Remote working opportunities and flexible working times, so you can combine your demanding work with your personal goals
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and Financial Wellness tool
  • Company-paid life insurance policy, long-term disability (LTD), and short-term disability (STD) coverage
  • Wellbeing apps, including Rightway, Headspace and Wellhub
  • Training and development opportunities to advance your career
  • President’s Club for the highest performing salespeople and overachievers
  • An amazing culture powered by a workplace run on trust, empowerment, and feedback with a positive, inspiring working atmosphere
  • A highly motivated team that is already looking forward to your support in developing strategies and achieving common goals, together with you!
