jobs.title: Head of Marketing - Remote, USA
jobs.excerpt: Who we are:Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory.
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.

Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.

About the team:

Formic's Marketing Team is the growth engine behind our commercial expansion. We move fast, experiment boldly, and build systems that scale. We work in close lockstep with Sales, RevOps, and Leadership to generate pipeline, sharpen our message, and get in front of the right manufacturers at the right time. This team is small, high-impact, and driven - and we're looking for someone who can match that energy.

About this role:

As our Head of Marketing, you will build, optimize, and lead a scalable engine for creating demand and qualified pipeline. You will own how Formic shows up in the market, how we identify and reach the manufacturers we can help, and how we turn that engagement into high quality opportunities for Sales.

This is a broad, hands-on role spanning Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering and managing a team to deliver across those areas. You'll bring those capabilities together around a common goal: creating qualified pipeline and quantifying through data and insights what's driving it. As Formic grows, you'll help determine how the team and these capabilities evolve.

We're looking for someone who combines creativity with operating rigor. You'll set strategy, but you'll stay close enough to the work to understand what's actually happening. You'll establish clear priorities, ownership, and metrics, and make decisions based on results. When something works, you'll scale it. When it doesn't, you'll change it or stop doing it.

You'll also build and develop the team around you. That means setting clear expectations, delegating real ownership, coaching people to get better, and holding the team accountable for results. We want a leader who welcomes challenges, seeks out evidence that their assumptions may be wrong, and changes course when the data or the team tells them something different.

This is a builder role. One day you might be sharpening Formic's positioning; the next, reviewing pipeline performance with Sales, coaching an SDR, digging into why a campaign isn't converting, or working with a GTM Engineer to test a completely different way of reaching manufacturers. You should be equally comfortable asking "What should we try?" and "Did it work?"

We’re not looking for a standard B2B marketing playbook or activity for activity’s sake. We’re looking for a Head of Marketing who creates focus from ambiguity, turns experiments into learning, and builds repeatable systems that drive measurable business results.

You’ll bring a healthy appetite for the unconventional—challenging how things have always been done, proposing bold ideas, and testing them intelligently. We want the kind of imagination that makes people stop, pay attention, and think differently about industrial automation.

The next great idea in industrial marketing probably sounds a little crazy. Good. We want to hear it. Help us make industrial robotics impossible to ignore.

You will own the engine that feeds our sales and deployments.

In this role you will:

Own Brand & Marketing

  • Own Formic's marketing strategy and how we show up in the market.
  • Develop and continually sharpen our positioning, messaging, and story.
  • Translate Formic's technology, business model, and customer value proposition into messaging that resonates with manufacturers and their economic buyers.
  • Own content, creative, video, website, customer stories, events, campaigns, thought leadership, PR, product marketing, and other channels that build awareness and demand.
  • Develop differentiated messaging across industries, use cases, personas, and stages of the buying journey.
  • Demonstrated ability to conceive and execute original, unconventional marketing campaigns that break through industry norms, capture attention, and produce measurable business impact.
  • Turn customer outcomes, deployments, product capabilities, and what we're learning in the field into compelling content.
  • Build Formic's brand within manufacturing while ensuring our marketing investments support clear commercial objectives.

Own Demand & Pipeline Generation

  • Own the creation of qualified pipelines across Marketing, lead generation, SDR/outbound, ABM, events, paid, organic, partnerships, and emerging channels.
  • Establish clear pipeline goals and build repeatable systems to identify, engage, and qualify manufacturers that fit Formic's ideal customer profile, optimizing channel mix, conversion, and resources.
  • Lead and develop our Sales Development function, including targeting, prospecting strategy, messaging, sequencing, coaching, productivity, and performance.
  • Establish clear funnel definitions, ownership, lead routing, and follow-up processes to ensure every source of inbound and outbound interest is captured, acted upon, and effectively handed off to Sales.
  • Partner closely with Sales and RevOps on territory priorities, pipeline needs, lead quality, conversion, and feedback from the market.
  • Measure pipeline contribution, progression, conversion, and cost by source and channel, connecting marketing investments to closed-won revenue and informing where to invest, optimize, or stop.

Build Our GTM Innovation Capability

  • Lead our GTM Engineering capability, using AI, automation, data, enrichment, personalization, and emerging technologies to improve how we identify, reach, engage, and qualify potential customers.
  • Own the effectiveness and evolution of our marketing technology ecosystem, including CRM integrations, outbound platforms, lead routing, data quality, attribution, and reporting, in partnership with Sales and RevOps.
  • Build and optimize scalable systems for account identification, segmentation, prospecting, personalization, campaign execution, and lead management.
  • Evaluate existing tools and workflows, identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, integrate, consolidate, or eliminate work rather than defaulting to additional tools or headcount.
  • Drive disciplined experimentation across channels, technologies, data sources, and approaches, establishing clear hypotheses, measurable outcomes, and decisions about what to scale, change, or stop.
  • Ensure our GTM infrastructure is reliable, documented, and maintainable, with clear ownership, appropriate data governance, and minimal dependency on any single person or external partner.

Own the Funnel and the Numbers

  • Establish clear visibility into the entire funnel, from target account through qualified opportunity, pipeline progression, and revenue.
  • Define and own a focused set of metrics that measure pipeline creation, conversion, velocity, cost, channel effectiveness, and commercial impact.
  • Partner with Sales and RevOps to ensure reliable data, consistent reporting, and a shared understanding of performance.
  • Establish a disciplined operating cadence that translates performance insights into decisions about strategy, priorities, budget, and resources, holding the organization accountable for outcomes rather than activity.

Create Focus and Accountability

  • Translate broad company objectives into clear priorities, ownership, expectations, and measurable outcomes that connect the team's work to business goals.
  • Make disciplined decisions about priorities and resources, challenging assumptions, stopping initiatives that aren't delivering results, and adapting as we learn.
  • Stay close enough to the work to identify problems early, remove obstacles, and hold people accountable without becoming a bottleneck to execution.
  • Foster a culture of transparency, constructive challenge, and open communication about performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and lessons learned.
  • Establish accountability for external agencies, contractors, and technology partners, including deliverables, performance, costs, documentation, and continuity, while building sustainable processes that preserve institutional knowledge and support organizational change.

Build and Lead the Team

  • Lead and align a multidisciplinary organization spanning Marketing, content and creative, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering around shared commercial goals.
  • Build a high-performing team by establishing clear expectations, delegating meaningful ownership, coaching and developing talent, and addressing performance gaps directly.
  • Assess existing capabilities, recognize and develop the strengths of the people already here, and determine what additional skills and resources we'll need as we grow.
  • Hire thoughtfully and build organizational capabilities that create leverage, rather than adding unnecessary layers or headcount.
  • Foster a culture of creativity, curiosity, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement, where people feel empowered to challenge assumptions and solve problems.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Experience building and leading Marketing, Growth, Demand Generation, or similarly broad functions in high-growth B2B companies, with measurable commercial results.
  • A track record of building, improving, and scaling marketing and pipeline-generation systems, not simply inheriting and managing established operations.
  • Deep understanding of B2B demand generation, funnel economics, segmentation, conversion, attribution, and how Marketing, SDR, and Sales work together to create and convert pipeline.
  • Experience developing differentiated positioning and messaging for complex products, markets, and buying decisions.
  • Strong technical fluency and demonstrated experience evaluating, integrating, and optimizing marketing technology, data, automation, and AI-enabled GTM systems, with the ability to diagnose problems and make informed architectural decisions.
  • An AI-native mindset, with demonstrated ability to apply emerging technologies, experiment rigorously, evaluate results, and turn successful approaches into scalable capabilities.
  • Strong people leadership, including building and developing teams, delegating meaningful ownership, addressing performance gaps, and leading effectively through growth and organizational change.
  • An operating style that combines creativity, analytical rigor, intellectual flexibility, and accountability, with the judgment to challenge assumptions, make difficult tradeoffs, and change course when evidence warrants it.
  • The ability to operate strategically and tactically, creating clarity from ambiguity, communicating effectively across functions, and staying close enough to execution to understand and solve problems.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience in manufacturing, industrial automation, robotics, industrial technology, or similarly complex B2B markets with long sales cycles and multiple decision-makers.
  • Experience directly building or leading SDR organizations, including account-based and territory-based outbound strategies.
  • Experience building or leading GTM Engineering, Growth Engineering, or similar technical growth capabilities.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, Formic has a marketing and pipeline-generation engine that we understand, measure, and know how to scale.

We know who we should target, how to reach them, which messages resonate, which channels create qualified opportunities, what those opportunities cost, and where we should invest next.

There is clear ownership across the funnel. Marketing, lead generation, Sales Development, and GTM Engineering operate as one connected organization, with a tight feedback loop into Sales. The team knows what matters and what it's accountable for.

Experiments have hypotheses and measurable outcomes. Successful ideas become repeatable systems. Unsuccessful ones produce learning and stop consuming resources. Decisions about priorities, budget, and headcount are grounded in results.

Our marketing and GTM infrastructure is reliable, integrated, and well understood. We have confidence in our data, clear accountability for lead management, and systems that the team can operate and improve independently. Technology and vendor decisions are deliberate, economically justified, and aligned with our commercial priorities.

Most importantly, Sales has a consistent and growing flow of qualified opportunities, and we can explain what is creating them.

That's the engine you'll own.

Our Total Rewards:

At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:

  • Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors
  • Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles
  • Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available
  • Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most
  • Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan
  • Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup
  • Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses
  • Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy

Compensation Philosophy

Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.

Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.

Compensation Range:
$145,000—$220,000 USD

What we look for:

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!

  • Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.
  • Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.
  • Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.
  • Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.
  • Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.
  • One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

Equal Opportunity Employment:

Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to .

AI Use:

At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked here.

Overview:

We’re on a mission to modernize insurance, making it simpler, more accessible, and customer-first. The insurance industry is a $1T market that has remained largely untouched by the digital revolution, and PolicyMe is here to change that. As a remote-first, Toronto-based startup with big ambitions, we’re looking for a Business Development Representative to help us build the future of insurance in Canada and beyond.

About This Role:

As a Business Development Representative (BDR), you’ll be at the heart of PolicyMe’s growth engine. You’ll manage a mix of inbound and outbound engagement, connecting with people who’ve already shown interest, from quote requests, started applications, to approved clients and helping move them forward in their insurance journey.
You’ll do initial outreach on inbound deals, convert incomplete applications into completed policies, and re-engage stale portions of the funnel. You’ll also qualify new clients, pack advisor calendars with high-quality meetings, and help optimize conversion throughout the funnel.
This is an established role within our Business Development team, where you’ll help scale a proven function and extend its impact. You’ll support ongoing experiments, refine strategies, and codify best practices to drive efficiency and results. Your insights and feedback will directly shape how we optimize lead conversion, outreach, and engagement at scale.
Success in this role requires curiosity, urgency, and a growth mindset. You’ll adapt your approach based on client feedback and data, continuously learning and improving how you connect with leads.
Top performers in this role will have the opportunity to pursue licensing and grow into a licensed Insurance Advisor position.

What you'll be doing:

  • Engage and qualify inbound leads through phone calls, emails, and text to understand their needs, determine fit, book meetings and move them toward a sale.
  • Operate with urgency to contact new leads quickly, follow up consistently, and manage a high volume of quality outreach.
  • Own outreach to inbound and warm outbound segments. You will contact clients who’ve requested quotes, started applications, or been approved.
  • Convert incomplete applications into active opportunities and help clients finish their purchase journey by scheduling meetings or transferring to an advisor.
  • Re-engage stalled or unresponsive leads to keep the pipeline healthy and full.
  • Keep your CRM (HubSpot) organized and up-to-date with detailed notes, ensuring seamless handoffs and visibility.
  • Work closely with the Advisor and Operations teams to optimize lead nurturing strategies and conversion processes.
  • Meet or exceed monthly conversion and engagement targets.
  • Represent PolicyMe in a professional and client-centric manner.
  • Analyze data to identify trends and suggest improvements to outreach strategies.

What we're looking for:

  • Experience or strong interest in sales, business develop or client facing roles. (This role is open to new & recent grads!)
  • A bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, economics, finance or any STEM field
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to connect quickly and adapt your approach.
  • Tech savvy and adaptable, comfortable learning new systems and making adjustments based on data and feedback.
  • Experience in engaging inbound or outbound leads is considered an asset.
  • Comfortable working in a CRM (we use HubSpot) and managing detailed follow ups.

About the job

The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms.

  • Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout.

  • Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures.

  • Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions.

  • Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock.

  • Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage.

  • Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks.

  • Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations.

  • Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment.

  • Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats.

  • Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus.

  • Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

  • Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles.

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.

  • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones.

About You

You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:

  • Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website.

  • Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms.

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @ or @

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

This role runs the operating system behind DataCore's revenue engine: the martech stack, data, routing, and reporting that connect marketing activity to pipeline and revenue across a channel-only go-to-market. Based in the UK, you work across EMEA and Americas time zones as the operational partner to revenue marketing, RevOps, sales, and the channel team. We're looking for a revenue-minded marketing operations leader who thinks in systems and owns the numbers the business runs on. You've run the full modern revenue stack in a B2B technology company, you're as comfortable in Salesforce and SQL as you are in a pipeline review with sales leadership, and you build AI-assisted workflows yourself. You treat data hygiene as non-negotiable and see marketing operations as the link between marketing spend and revenue.

What Success Looks Like

Immediate Mandate (First 90 Days)

  • Audit the full martech stack and data flows, and deliver a consolidation and remediation plan.

  • Clean and connect CRM, marketing automation, and intent data with RevOps.

  • Agree the shared funnel and qualified pipeline definitions with sales and RevOps.

  • Stand up the v1 pipeline and campaign performance dashboard.

  • Document lead, account, and partner routing, and the hand-off SLA.

6-12 Months

  • The stack is consolidated, integrated, and clean, with a clear owner and cost line for every tool.

  • Marketing and sales report against one funnel and one set of definitions.

  • A channel-aware attribution model is live and trusted by Finance and sales leadership.

  • Weekly, monthly, and board reporting runs without manual reassembly.

  • AI workflows for enrichment, QA, and reporting are in production with clear governance.

  • Routing to sellers and partners holds to SLA, with partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline visible end to end.

Key Responsibilities

Duties:

  • Own the full marketing technology stack end to end: CRM, marketing automation, ABM and intent, enrichment, routing, attribution, web analytics, webinar and event platforms, and the partner relationship management (PRM) integration.

  • Run the stack as a revenue system, with every tool tied to a funnel stage and a measurable contribution to pipeline, and run regular audits to consolidate overlap and manage vendor contracts and cost.

  • Own the marketing data foundation with Sales Ops, including field definitions, account and contact hierarchies, enrichment, deduplication, and the data model that reporting and AI workflows depend on.

  • Define and maintain one shared funnel with Sales Ops and sales, from engagement to lead, sales acceptance, and pipeline, so marketing and sales report against the same numbers.

  • Own lead and account routing end to end, including routing to the right DataCore seller and registered partner, deal registration data flows, and the marketing-to-sales-engineering hand-off SLA.

  • Build the channel-aware attribution model, crediting partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline as first-class revenue, and keep it trusted by Finance and sales leadership.

  • Build and maintain the KPI dashboards and reporting cadence, from weekly campaign and channel performance to monthly executive and quarterly board reporting on pipeline, coverage, CAC, and marketing contribution to revenue.

  • Provide the data inputs for the growth forecast and pipeline coverage models, working with Revenue Marketing and Finance.

  • Own campaign operations, building, QA-ing, and launching campaigns with consistent UTM conventions, campaign taxonomy, and tracking across every channel and region.

  • Operationalize ABM and intent data by maintaining the 6sense integration, account scoring, and buying-group data, so ABM, sellers, and partners act on the same signals.

  • Build and govern AI workflows across the stack, including Clay enrichment, AI agents for QA and reporting, and clear rules for where AI output can act without human review.

  • Own data privacy and consent across regions, including UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and CAN-SPAM, working closely with legal.

  • Document the operations playbook, definitions, and SLAs, and train the team so the function doesn't depend on any one person.

  • Partner across demand generation, ABM, field marketing, digital, and the GTM engineering team as the operational backbone for the whole marketing organisation.

Experience & Education

  • AI-first problem solving is the core requirement for this role: you reach for AI first, not last, to think through and solve real problems, treat AI as a digital co-worker rather than an occasional tool, and can point to how you've actually done it. This isn't optional, and it isn't just familiarity with the tools.

  • 7+ years in marketing operations or revenue operations in B2B technology, with deep ownership of the martech stack and CRM.

  • Salesforce fluency is a must, with administrator-level comfort in campaigns, objects, flows, and reporting, plus hands-on ownership of a marketing automation platform such as Marketo or HubSpot.

  • Hands-on experience with a modern revenue stack beyond CRM and MAP, including ABM and intent (6sense or Demandbase), enrichment and data orchestration (Clay, ZoomInfo), routing (LeanData or equivalent), and conversational or web tools.

  • Strong SQL and BI fluency (Looker, Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent), able to build and maintain dashboards without relying on a data team.

  • Real experience building attribution models, including multi-touch or partner attribution.

  • Experience with a CDP or data warehouse layer, such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Segment.

  • Working knowledge of UK GDPR and EU GDPR and how they shape consent, data handling, and campaign operations.

  • UK-based, with regular overlap with US Eastern time.

  • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience in a channel-led or partner-heavy GTM motion, including PRM integration (Impartner, Allbound, or Salesforce PRM) and deal registration data flows.

  • Experience consolidating or migrating a martech stack, beyond operating one already in place.

  • Hands-on experience building AI agents or automations that run in production, using tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, n8n, Workato, or Zapier.

  • Experience with revenue attribution platforms such as HockeyStack, Dreamdata, or Marketo Measure.

  • Background in infrastructure, storage, cloud, or data software.

  • Experience in a PE- or growth-equity-backed company, where reporting has to hold up to board and investor scrutiny.

Physical Demands

Position Summary:

Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA testing, focused on changing the management of disease in reproductive health, oncology, and organ transplantation. Signatera is a personalized, tumor-informed test for molecular residual disease (MRD) assessment and surveillance monitoring in patients previously diagnosed with cancer.

The Associate Director / Director of Product Management, Signatera Heme will own the product strategy and roadmap for Signatera in hematologic malignancies, starting with multiple myeloma and lymphomas. This person will work in a highly matrixed environment with the Foresight BU, R&D, Lab Operations, Software Engineering, Medical Affairs, Marketing, Business Development, and Regulatory. The role combines product management, market entry as a laboratory developed test (LDT), evidence generation, analytics, and clinical trial product support, including trials run under IUO and IVD pathways.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute the Signatera product roadmap for hematologic malignancies, beginning with multiple myeloma and lymphomas (for example, DLBCL, follicular, mantle cell, and Hodgkin lymphoma) and extending to additional heme indications.
  • Lead market entry planning for Signatera in heme as a laboratory developed test (LDT), including clinical validation requirements, CLIA and state requirements, market access/reimbursement and payer considerations, and launch readiness with Lab Operations, Regulatory, Medical, commercial and Marketing.
  • Define product requirements for blood-based malignancies with R&D, Lab Operations, and Software Engineering, including assay, sample type, workflow, and reporting needs.
  • Lead product support for clinical trials using Signatera in heme, including IUO use in studies with pharma and academic partners, and the path toward IVD and regulated use.
  • Partner with Regulatory, Clinical, and Business Development on trial start-up, study requirements, and pharma and companion diagnostic opportunities.
  • Build product performance metrics and dashboards. Analyze test volume, adoption, ordering patterns, turnaround time, and retention. Use the results to prioritize improvements.
  • Partner with Medical Affairs and Clinical on evidence generation strategy and execution. Areas of collaboration include identifying clinical gaps, designing studies, working with investigators and trial partners, and planning publications and congress presentations.
  • Guide product development for Signatera Genome in heme, including whole genome sequencing technology, phased variants, and structural variants. Work with R&D and Bioinformatics to define how these features improve tumor tracking and MRD sensitivity in heme malignancies.
  • Conduct Voice of Customer interviews, market research, and competitive and market intelligence in hematologic oncology.
  • Engage with key opinion leaders, advisory boards, and congresses (for example, ASH, EHA, and ASCO). Gather insights to guide product decisions.
  • Work with Marketing on product positioning, launch plans, pricing, and key collateral.

  • Experience bringing a molecular test to market as an LDT, including clinical validation and laboratory requirements.
  • Experience designing or supporting clinical evidence generation, such as clinical validation studies, retrospective studies, or prospective trials.
  • Prior KOL engagement and external customer facing experience preferred.
  • 30-40% travel for advisory boards, congresses, and customer meetings.

Knowledge, Skill, and Abilities:

Technical

  • Understanding of MRD in multiple myeloma and lymphomas, including how blood-based MRD testing fits withing current bone marrow and imaging-based MRD assessment paradigms.
  • Understanding of how somatic variants are detected in whole genome sequencing and how they support MRD tracking in heme tumors.
  • Understanding of LDT market entry requirements and the evidence needed for clinical adoption and payer coverage.
  • Ability to translate customer and clinical needs into clear product requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills. Able to build metrics, interpret data, and present findings.

  • Proficiency with MS Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Behavioral

  • Strong written and oral communication skills and ability to function effectively in a highly matrixed cross functional environment.

The Role

We are looking for a high-judgment, process-driven Financial Operations Managerto lead our Money Movement and Payroll Settlement team. In this role, you will own the engine of our business: ensuring funds are debited from client accounts accurately and delivered into the bank accounts of thousands of workers seamlessly and on time.

You will manage a daily operational team, oversee multi-million-dollar banking and ACH transmission workflows, lead exception handling (returns, reversals, NSF, and disputes), and partner directly with Risk Operations and banking partners to scale our treasury and clearing infrastructure.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead, mentor, and scale a team of Financial Operations Specialists responsible for day-to-day payroll funding, direct deposit transmission, and exception processing.

  • Oversee end-to-end clearing timelines across multiple banking rails (Same-Day ACH, Standard ACH, Wire, RTP, and FedNow).

  • Ensure critical cut-off deadlines (Federal Reserve / ODFI / RDFI windows) are met with zero tolerance for delayed worker payroll disbursements.

  • Monitor real-time account balances, debit settlements, credit batches, and intraday clearing files (NACHA, ISO 20022, proprietary bank APIs).

  • Own the operational resolution of ACH returns (e.g., R01 NSF, R08 stop payment, R03 unauthorized account), credit reversals, trace requests, and payroll adjustments.

  • Implement proactive fraud, exposure, and NSF-monitoring protocols to mitigate credit risk between debit settlement and credit disbursement.

  • Serve as the senior point of escalation for high-value funding failures, off-cycle emergency payroll runs, and banking transmission disruptions.

  • Maintain daily three-way reconciliation across client payroll records, internal ledger balances, and bank statements.

  • Partner with Corporate Accounting and Treasury to track settlement float, collateral accounts, and clearing reserves.

  • Design and enforce strict operational controls (Maker-Checker protocols, dual authorization, and change-log auditing) in compliance with SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2, and NACHA rules.

  • Partner closely with Product and Core Platform Engineering to translate manual financial workflows into automated software tools.

  • Drive root-cause analyses on recurring transaction failures, latency issues, or bank API errors to continuously improve straight-through processing (STP) rates.

  • Maintain relationships with tier-1 partner banks and payment processors to optimize cut-off windows, fee structures, and clearing speeds.

  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

About Hello Heart:

Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.

We’re an AI company focused exclusively on heart health, building a platform that predicts and prevents cardiac events before they happen—identifying risk up to 10 days in advance versus 10 years in traditional clinical models.

This is already working at scale. Hello Heart has been shown to reduce inpatient hospital days by 47% and deliver ~$1,800 in annual savings per member. Hello Heart is the cardiac prevention partner to over 80% of large U.S. health plans and serves hundreds of public and private employers.

We’re defining how the #1 cause of death—heart disease—is managed in the AI era. Join us.

About the role:

Hello Heart is looking for a strategic and commercially minded Senior Director, Actuarial Services to lead actuarial strategy, health economic analyses, and financial value demonstration across our business.

In this highly visible role, you will serve as Hello Heart's actuarial expert, translating complex healthcare data into clear, compelling insights that demonstrate the clinical and financial value of our heart health solution. You will partner with customers, consultants, health plans, and internal stakeholders to strengthen our value proposition, support commercial growth, and inform strategic decision-making.

Reporting into our VP, Commercial Actuary, you will collaborate closely with Medical Affairs, Consultant Relations, Sales, Growth, Customer Success, and Finance. You will lead health economic research, develop risk-based pricing models, oversee performance guarantees and related reserves, and represent Hello Heart in high-impact client and consultant engagements.

This is an opportunity to shape how we measure, communicate, and deliver value while advancing our mission to empower people to understand and improve their heart health.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with Sales, Consultant Relations, and Customer Success to strengthen proposals and communicate Hello Heart's economic value.
  • As a client-facing member of the team, join client and consultant calls, performance reviews, and renewal value conversations, providing strategy, decisions, and key input as a credible face of Hello Heart.
  • Advocate for sound actuarial practices, appropriate methodologies, and effective processes that support high-quality analyses and informed decision-making.
  • Serve as one of Hello Heart's primary actuarial subject matter experts, providing strategic guidance on healthcare economics, financial outcomes, pricing, and market opportunities.
  • Lead health economic studies, cost savings analyses, and outcomes research that quantify the impact of Hello Heart and support commercial growth.
  • Leverage medical claims, pharmacy claims, and other large datasets to evaluate healthcare utilization, medication adherence, costs, and financial outcomes.
  • Develop and maintain competitive performance guarantee offerings, assess associated financial risks, oversee reserve requirements, and educate internal stakeholders.
  • Develop risk-based pricing approaches and support value-based contracting and specialty incentive opportunities.
  • Present actuarial and health economic findings to customers, consultants, payers, industry audiences, other external stakeholders, and at conferences.
  • Serve as the primary actuarial contact for independent cost savings studies, research collaborations, and analyses conducted with consultants and external partners.
  • Evaluate the anticipated clinical and financial impact of new products and services, identify market opportunities, and provide actuarial input into strategic planning.
  • Develop executive-ready presentations, research materials, and publications that make complex statistical findings accessible and actionable.
  • Track healthcare market dynamics, competitor trends, Medicare Advantage quality measures, and emerging reimbursement models to inform business decisions.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of actuarial experience within healthcare, health insurance, or a related healthcare organization, including experience conducting health economic and financial analyses.
  • Client-facing or sales-support experience, such as in consulting or a startup, with a track record of presenting analyses to customers, consultants, or executives.
  • A credible storyteller and strong listener who builds trust quickly.
  • Deep knowledge of actuarial principles, healthcare economics, risk assessment, and statistical methodologies, with the ability to apply findings to commercial and strategic decisions.
  • Proficiency in R and experience analyzing large medical and pharmacy claims datasets, including paid and allowed amounts, healthcare utilization, and medication adherence measures.
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage artificial intelligence tools and agents to streamline research, analysis, reporting, and complex workflows while critically evaluating outputs for accuracy and reliability.
  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Actuarial Science, or a related field.
  • Associate of the Society of Actuaries (ASA) or Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA) credential.
  • Experience developing or evaluating healthcare cost savings studies, financial outcomes research, performance guarantees, and risk-based pricing models.
  • Understanding of risk adjustment, Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, healthcare quality metrics, and related audit processes.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex actuarial and statistical concepts into compelling presentations for executive and external audiences.
  • Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and independently drive high-impact initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to travel up to 20% of the time.

jobs.title: CONTRÔLEUR(SE) DE GESTION JUNIOR – H/F – DAKAR / CASABLANCA / MARRAKECH
jobs.excerpt: À PROPOS D’EBHIEBHI – Entrepreneur Business Hub International – accompagne des entreprises partenaires dans leur développement.
jobs.description:
À PROPOS D’EBHI

EBHI – Entrepreneur Business Hub International – accompagne des entreprises partenaires dans leur développement. Nous les aidons à se structurer, à renforcer leur organisation et leur pilotage, et à constituer des équipes compétentes pour soutenir leur croissance.

Dans ce cadre, nous mettons à disposition de nos partenaires des talents qualifiés, recrutés et accompagnés par EBHI, qui interviennent au cœur de leurs enjeux opérationnels et financiers.

L’ENTREPRISE PARTENAIRE

Nous recrutons pour l’un de nos partenaires, une entreprise en croissance basée en France qui opère un réseau de boutiques, une activité parfums, une activité de vente en ligne et une activité de vente en gros (B2B), accompagnées de projets de travaux et d’aménagement liés à son développement.

Pour renforcer le pilotage de ses performances, notre partenaire crée un poste de Contrôleur(se) de Gestion, exercé à distance depuis Dakar, Casablanca ou Marrakech, en lien direct avec sa Direction en France.

LE POSTE

Vous êtes les yeux de la Direction sur les chiffres. Votre rôle : savoir, jour après jour, quelle boutique, quel produit et quel canal gagne ou perd de l’argent, repérer les dépenses inutiles et proposer des actions concrètes.

Nous ne cherchons pas une personne qu’il faudra suivre en permanence : nous cherchons un profil junior, mais déjà opérationnel, capable de travailler en autonomie, d’aller chercher l’information à la source et de rendre compte de manière claire et régulière.

VOS MISSIONS PRINCIPALES

Rentabilité – boutique par boutique, produit par produit, canal par canal

  • Calculer et suivre la rentabilité de chaque boutique : chiffre d’affaires, marge, charges directes (loyer, personnel, énergie…), contribution au résultat.

  • Mesurer la rentabilité des parfums par référence et par gamme : coût de revient, marge, rotation des stocks.

  • Suivre la performance de chaque canal : boutiques, e-commerce, vente en gros.

  • Identifier les points de vente, produits ou postes en perte et proposer des plans d’action.

Contrôle des dépenses et des coûts

  • Vérifier la cohérence des factures fournisseurs et des dépenses engagées : est-ce justifié, au bon prix, conforme à ce qui a été commandé ?

  • Suivre les charges fixes : loyers, contrats, abonnements, frais généraux.

  • Repérer les dépenses inutiles, les doublons et les dérives, et proposer des économies chiffrées.

  • Suivre les budgets et les dépenses des travaux et aménagements (devis, avancement, écarts).

Pilotage quotidien et reporting

  • Mettre en place et tenir un suivi quotidien de l’activité (ventes, encaissements, dépenses).

  • Construire les tableaux de bord et les ratios clés : marge, panier moyen, coût du loyer rapporté au CA, masse salariale / CA, rotation des stocks, point mort par boutique…

  • Produire un reporting hebdomadaire et mensuel clair à destination de la Direction.

  • Participer à l’élaboration du budget, au suivi des écarts et à la trésorerie prévisionnelle, en lien avec la comptabilité.

  • Fiabiliser les données et améliorer progressivement les outils et les process de suivi.

PROFIL RECHERCHÉ

  • Formation : Bac+4/5 en contrôle de gestion, finance, audit ou comptabilité (école de commerce, master CCA, ISCAE, ENCG ou équivalent).

  • Expérience : 2 ans minimum en contrôle de gestion, audit ou analyse financière (hors stages). Une expérience en retail, distribution, parfumerie / cosmétique ou e-commerce est un vrai plus.

  • Outils : très bonne maîtrise d’Excel (tableaux croisés dynamiques, RECHERCHEX / RECHERCHEV, formules avancées). Power BI, Power Query ou un ERP / logiciel de caisse sont appréciés.

  • Compétences : bases solides en comptabilité générale et analytique, calcul de coûts de revient et de marges, lecture d’un compte de résultat.

  • Savoir-être : très motivé(e), autonome, rigoureux(se), curieux(se), à l’aise sur le terrain comme devant un tableau de chiffres. Vous savez expliquer simplement vos analyses à des non-financiers.

  • Langues : français courant indispensable ; l’anglais est un plus.

CE QUI FERA LA DIFFÉRENCE

  • Vous avez déjà suivi la rentabilité de plusieurs points de vente ou de plusieurs activités.

  • Vous avez déjà identifié des économies concrètes grâce à une analyse des dépenses ou des factures.

  • Vous avez construit vous-même un tableau de bord ou un reporting utilisé par une direction.

  • Vous avez envie de grandir vite dans un environnement entrepreneurial où l’on vous confie de vraies responsabilités.

CE QUE NOUS VOUS OFFRONS

  • Un poste créé pour vous, en lien direct avec la Direction de l’entreprise partenaire.

  • Une vision complète d’une entreprise multi-activités : retail, parfums, e-commerce, B2B, travaux.

  • Une vraie liberté pour structurer la fonction et ses outils.

  • Une forte montée en compétences et des perspectives d’évolution au sein de l’écosystème EBHI et de ses partenaires.

CONDITIONS

  • Statut : Indépendant(e) – facturation mensuelle

  • Localisation : au choix : Dakar (Sénégal), Casablanca ou Marrakech (Maroc) – pour une entreprise partenaire basée en France

  • Rémunération : selon profil et expérience

  • Disponibilité : dès que possible

PROCESSUS DE RECRUTEMENT

  • Candidature via ce formulaire : CV à jour et réponses aux questions de présélection, dont une courte vidéo.

  • Pour les profils retenus : un cas pratique de contrôle de gestion (analyse de rentabilité et de dépenses sur données réelles simplifiées).

  • Un entretien final avec EBHI et la Direction de l’entreprise partenaire.

Rejoignez EBHI !

... Et mettez les chiffres au service des décisions de notre partenaire !

jobs.title: Senior Workforce IAM Engineer
jobs.excerpt: College Board – Technology – Workforce IAMLocation: This is a remote role.
jobs.description:
College Board – Technology – Workforce IAM

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The Workforce Identity and Access Management (WIAM) team is the identity control plane for College Board's enterprise. The team owns the full workforce identity lifecycle, from onboarding and provisioning through access governance, certification, and offboarding, and operates the platforms that enforce authentication, authorization, and privileged access management across the organization.

WIAM's work spans six capability pillars: identity onboarding, provisioning, authentication and authorization, credential management, governance and compliance, and identity offboarding. Each pillar has a named engineer accountable for its maturity, its roadmap, and the controls that run inside it. The team is the primary owner of College Board's enterprise IGA platform and PAM infrastructure, and it partners closely with Talent, ISGRC, and security peer teams to ensure identity services are reliable, auditable, and aligned to Zero Trust principles.

The team operates at the intersection of security rigor and user experience; the controls WIAM builds directly affect how every College Board employee accesses systems and data every day. As College Board's workforce has grown and its cloud and SaaS footprint has expanded, WIAM's scope has grown to match: centralizing more applications, automating more lifecycle actions, and governing an increasingly complex mix of human and non-human identities.

About the Opportunity

As a Senior Engineer on the WIAM team, you are a hands-on identity engineer who owns the Governance and Compliance pillar and is accountable for it meeting its goals. The pillar covers the governance of access and identities in the IGA platform across human, service, and AI agent identities (currently in the building phase), including access reviews, security attestations, account reviews, least-privilege enforcement, segregation of duties, and account ownership and accountability. You ensure the access sent to reviewers is accurate and understandable, that reviews run on schedule, and that each produces clear, auditable evidence. While each review has an owner, you administer and facilitate how it is implemented, advising on feasibility, scheduling, notifications and communications, the evidence produced, and what the platform can give the reviewers. You are directly involved in how AI agents are integrated into the IGA platform, so they meet the same level of accountability through defined owners, lifecycle states, and reviewable access, while minimizing business impact when access is removed.

You also work as part of our broader WIAM team, where all engineers share the workload across our applications (AD, Entra ID, Okta OIG, CyberArk, and 1Password). That work includes access provisioning, identity management, setting up applications and integrations, building and maintaining automations (PowerShell, Okta Workflows, ADManager Plus, and other automation tools), maintaining vaults in CyberArk, and various other tasks. You bring a governance lens to all of it, asking what internal and external auditors will want from each process and making sure it is there. The controls you build shape how every College Board employee reaches the systems and data they need to serve students.

In this role, you will:

Facilitate Certifications, Attestations, and Governance (35%)

  • Plan and forecast the year's review cycle in Okta, including annual recurring reviews and new work, while balancing other teams' capacity against compliance and external audit deadlines
  • Design, configure, launch, monitor, and close access reviews, account reviews, and security attestations in Okta across human, service, and AI agent identities, scoped so reviewers can make considered decisions while reducing review fatigue
  • Bring new account types into the recurring review cycle as they come into scope
  • Run the annual user access review cycle end to end, from scoping and reviewer assignment through remediation, closure, and delivery of the auditor reporting package against the use cases agreed upon with the audit owner
  • Fulfill evidence requests from internal College Board groups and external auditors by the agreed due date
  • Verify requirements and review data before launch, and bring any issues you spot to the review owner
  • Maintain the job guides and documentation that let another engineer run a review cycle correctly without you
  • Partner with Security, Risk, Audit, Technology and business teams to translate security, compliance and technical requirements into workable identity controls
  • Keep WIAM's practices aligned to College Board information security policy, tracking policy changes and flagging where team practice needs to move

Build and Enforce AI Governance (25%)

  • Integrate AI agent identities into the IGA platform as they come online, with defined owners, lifecycle states, and reviewable access
  • Define the ownership model for AI agents: who is accountable for an agent's access, and what happens when its purpose or owner changes
  • Bring AI agent identities under access review and least-privilege enforcement on the same cycle as human and service accounts
  • Govern the access AI tools and agents hold to College Board systems and data: what each can reach, who approved it, how it is reviewed, and how to revoke it
  • Build and run the attestation flows for AI tools as the organization adopts them, reusing patterns rather than rebuilding per tool
  • Partner with AI governance stakeholders and Risk Engineering so identity controls for agents are designed once and land in the right place

Build & Run Identity Services with Security in Mind (40%)

  • Work alongside the team on day-to-day identity engineering, including onboarding, offboarding, and access requests, asking what internal and external auditors will want from each and making sure it is there
  • Direct and review governance pillar work carried out by other engineers on the team, remaining accountable for the outcome
  • Establish and maintain account ownership and accountability across identity types: named owners and defined lifecycle states for human, service, and workload identities, extending to API identities as they come into scope
  • Enforce least privilege with exceptions documented and tracked
  • Monitor and correct any unintended changes between approved and actual entitlements across centralized applications
  • Automate enforcement and evidence with Okta Workflows and platform APIs
  • Measure the team's controls against recognized industry frameworks such as NIST, identify gaps, and propose how to close them
  • Report on the enforcement of the pillar's controls with documented, traceable data
  • Analyze access and entitlement data to support troubleshooting, audits, and continuous improvement
  • Participate in the team's on-call rotation, responding to identity platform incidents and following established escalation procedures

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • 5+ years of identity and access management and/or security engineering experience, including hands-on work with Active Directory, Entra ID, and Okta
  • Experience designing and running access reviews, certifications, or attestation campaigns at scale, including scoping, reviewer assignment, remediation, and closure, and delivering the evidence to internal or external auditors
  • Working knowledge of policy and compliance frameworks such as NIST, and the judgment to translate framework guidance into practical control requirements
  • Hands-on production experience with Okta, especially Okta Identity Governance and Okta Workflows
  • Experience with agentic AI governance: treating agents and workload identities as governed identities with owners, lifecycle states, and certifiable access
  • Solid grounding in identity and access standards (SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, SCIM) and in role- and attribute-based access control, SSO, MFA, and least privilege
  • A secure-by-design mindset, with security built in as a system is designed, and a habit of checking a system’s actual state rather than what the configuration screen reported and of tracing a number back to the record it came from
  • Strong written communication and the ability to see a control from the business and end-user perspective as well as the engineer's, including explain a control to someone who does not work in identity
  • Preferred: Experience as an IT auditor or in a GRC function, testing controls over identities, provisioning, and access
  • Preferred: Enterprise security certifications or recent coursework (e.g., CISSP, CISA, CRISC, Okta certifications, or similar)
  • Preferred: A working understanding of defense in depth and how to implement layered controls in practice

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Authorization to work in the United States for any employer
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than just a paycheck—we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation, grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $153,000 – $166,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront—rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

As a Senior Front End Developer at Lateral, you will:

  • Craft delightful digital experiences: Design, implement, and maintain front-end features using React and modern JavaScript/TypeScript. You’ll create reusable UI components and craft polished, responsive interfaces with a focus on quality

  • Collaborate & communicate: Work closely with designers, back-end developers, and product managers in an asynchronous workflow. You’ll regularly communicate with clients to clarify requirements, demo features, and ensure we’re building the right thing.

  • Lead and take ownership: As a senior member, you’ll drive projects from concept to completion. That means making technical decisions, outlining implementation plans, and seeing them through deployment. You’ll have the freedom to introduce new ideas and best practices that raise the bar for our front-end, whether it’s improving our build process or adopting an innovative UI approach – all justified by real benefit to the team and product.

  • Optimize, Iterate & improve: Involve yourself in brainstorming and technical discussions. Ensure our apps are fast, accessible, and reliable. You’ll profile and improve page load times, refine animations, and tackle browser-specific quirks so that every user gets a smooth experience. When issues arise, you’ll dive in to debug and fix them, striving for robust solutions that scale (and writing tests to prevent regressions

  • Mentor and learn: Guide and mentor junior developers by sharing your expertise and providing constructive feedback. At the same time, stay curious and keep up with industry trends, frameworks, and standards. You’ll be encouraged to continuously learn and bring in knowledge, evaluating new technologies thoughtfully to see if they can enhance our product or developer experience (we love learning, but avoid “innovation for innovation’s sake”). In short, you’ll help shape a culture of excellence, ownership, and growth on the team.

Example Projects You May Join:

  • Large scale B2B2C Commerce Platform: Help build a responsive, mobile-first experience for an international e-commerce client. For example, you might lead a dynamic multi-faceted search or a smooth checkout flow

  • Develop from scratch an application: Collaborate with a senior backend engineer/architect to build a modern application. You’ll be involved in everything from crafting components to API definition.

  • Real-Time Medical Dashboard: Develop front-end features for a real-time analytics dashboard for a pet healthcare client. You might use libraries like AGCharts to visualize large data sets, implement live updates via websockets, and ensure the interface remains highly performant and user-friendly.

Whatever the challenge, you’ll be building software that changes lives and moves industries forward.

How we measure success in this role

In the first two weeks

  • You've set up your development environment and tools.

  • You’ve pushed your first meaningful contribution (bugfix, UI tweak, or minor feature).

  • You’re familiar with our async workflows and communication style.

  • You’ve participated in your first client sync and started understanding the project's context.

In the first 3 months:

  • You’ve led development on a significant feature or initiative.

  • You’ve actively mentored a teammate or shared knowledge through code review or documentation.

  • You’ve authored or contributed to architectural decisions and design documents.

  • You’ve established trust with clients through clear communication and technical guidance.

  • You’ve improved performance, code structure, or tooling in meaningful ways.

After 3 months:

  • You’re recognized as a technical leader in your project or team.

  • You’ve initiated a broader improvement across projects (e.g., shared component library, new testing standard).

  • You’re frequently unblocking teammates, elevating code quality, and proactively identifying risks.

  • You balance speed and quality, delivering with care and clarity.

We measure success through:

  • The impact and scope of your technical contributions.

  • Your ability to lead initiatives, mentor others, and improve team practices.

  • Code quality, performance, and maintainability.

  • Positive feedback from peers, clients, and design/engineering leadership.

  • Your growth mindset, communication skills, and influence on team culture.

What We’re Looking For

We are seeking for team members who are both highly technical and deeply care about their craft and how the work gets done. You must bring:

  • 7+ years of professional front-end development experience building digital applications. Experience with modern Javascript libraries and tooling (e.g. React, npm, webpack...). Fluency in CSS and first-principles understanding front end technologies.

  • Proven ability tocraft, polish, delight, sweat the details.
    You have an eye for design and UX. Pixel-perfect isn’t just a phrase to you – you care about creating beautiful, intuitive interfaces that make users happy. An understanding of design principles and attention to details like accessibility and responsive layout is important.

  • Quality and reliability
    You take pride in building high-quality software. You’re diligent about testing and documentation, and you proactively debug issues before they become problems. ￼ Performance and browser compatibility matter to you – you know how to make a web app fast and handle the quirks of different environments ￼. Ultimately, you balance speed of delivery with maintainability, ensuring the code you ship today won’t be tech debt tomorrow.

  • Self-driven and accountable: You’re comfortable managing your own projects and time without heavy oversight. When you take on a task, we can count on you to see it through with a sense of ownership. You’re a proactive problem solver who can break down complex problems, propose solutions, and drive them to completion. We trust our team members to be “managers of one” who take initiative and deliver results.

  • Great communication and empathy are a must. You enjoy working closely with others, be it in pair programming, brainstorming with designers, or reviewing a teammate’s code. You can explain technical concepts clearly, listen to alternate viewpoints, and work together to find the best solutions. Our culture is about being kind, open, and constructive, so we’re looking for someone who lifts others up and thrives in a friendly, collaborative environment.

  • Remote work skills: Self-motivated and disciplined in a remote environment. You can manage your time, collaborate asynchronously, and aren’t afraid to ask questions or offer help across time zones.

Bonus points for:

  • Demonstrating craft

  • Design /delight sensibility

  • AI & Gen AI experience/tooling

  • Understanding Backend concepts

  • CSR/SSR

  • DevOps experience (continuous integration, hosting, etc.)

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Real Impact: You’ll work on meaningful products that make a measurable difference - from healthcare and commerce to sustainability and next-gen tech.

  • Remote-First, Office Friendly: Work from wherever you’re most productive - whether that’s your home, a co-working space, or one of our offices. We’re a remote-first company, but if you’re near an office, you’re welcome to drop in, collaborate in person, or work onsite regularly.

    We prioritize async collaboration, respect your time zone, and focus on outcomes over hours.

  • An Outstanding Team: Talented, kind, and hard-working people who care deeply about their craft - and about each other. No egos. No politics. Just professionals doing their best work.

  • Growth: You’ll be supported in growing your craft, exploring new paths, and stepping into greater responsibility - at your own pace

  • A Culture of Excellence: We care deeply about doing the right thing - for our clients, our team, and ourselves. No burnout. No crunch. Just high-quality work, delivered sustainably.

  • Variety & Stability: We’re profitable, independent, and over a decade strong. Yet every project brings a fresh challenge. You’ll never be bored here.

This Role Might Not Be for You

We want to respect your time by being clear about what this role isn’t. You should skip this opportunity if:

  • You prefer well defined structure. If you gravitate towards a clear hierarchy, well defined roles and swim lanes, you may find our self-managed style challenging.

  • Distributed work isn’t your thing. If you find async communication, design documentation and being proactive without a manager nearby difficult, our setup won’t suit you.

  • Feedback doesn't excite you. We’re obsessed with quality and believe in continuous improvement. That means we give feedback that’s sometimes nitpicky. If refining the work until it’s excellent feels over the top, you are likely going to find working here frustrating.

  • Change makes you uncomfortable. We’re scaling and maturing. That means not everything is perfect yet. Priorities shift. Processes evolve. If ambiguity is uncomfortable, this may feel bumpy.

However, If this sounds like fuel, we’d love to talk!

How to apply and what to expect in the interview process

01. Your work
Show us the work that reflects you at your best. We’ll look at depth, design thinking, and the logic behind your choices.

02. Lateral team fit
You’ll speak with our Talent team about your career direction, your motivators, and our plans ahead.

03. Work trial

You’ll tackle a take-home challenge that mirrors what we actually do.

04.Engineering deep dive
A collaborative session with our engineers.

05. Project fit
An interview focussed on prioritization, collaboration across disciplines, and how you handle the "messy middle".
